## 74. React Cheat Sheet

**Hooks at a glance:**

| Hook | Use for | Remember |
|---|---|---|
| `useState` | values that change and affect the UI | snapshot per render; updater `s => …` for queued updates; lazy init `useState(() => …)` |
| `useReducer` | related state with many update types | pure reducer; dispatch actions describing events |
| `useContext` / `use(Context)` | values needed deep in the tree | all readers re-render on change; split contexts |
| `useRef` | values that don't affect rendering; DOM nodes | changing `.current` doesn't re-render; not during render |
| `useEffect` | syncing with outside systems | deps = every reactive value read; cleanup; StrictMode double-run in dev |
| `useEffectEvent` | non-reactive logic inside effects | call only from effects; not a dependency |
| `useLayoutEffect` | measure then adjust before paint | blocks painting; use sparingly |
| `useMemo` / `useCallback` / `memo` | skip expensive work / keep references stable | measure first; the React Compiler does it automatically |
| `useTransition` / `useDeferredValue` | keep urgent updates responsive | not for input values themselves |
| `useId` | accessible ids matching server and client | not for list keys |
| `useSyncExternalStore` | subscribe to outside stores | `getSnapshot` must return a stable value |
| `useActionState` / `useFormStatus` / `useOptimistic` | form actions, pending state, optimistic UI | `useFormStatus` reads the parent form |
| `useImperativeHandle` | expose a few methods through a ref | `ref` is a normal prop in React 19 |

**Decision shortcuts:**

- Can it be computed from props or state? → compute it during render (not state, not an effect).
- Caused by a user action? → event handler. Must stay in sync with something outside React? → effect with cleanup.
- Reset a component when an id changes? → `key={id}`.
- Several components need the same state? → lift it to their closest common parent; many distant components → context or a store.
- Server data? → TanStack Query / router loaders / Server Components. URL-worthy state? → search params.
- Slow re-renders? → move state down, pass `children`, then `memo` / the Compiler; long lists → virtualise; big bundles → `lazy` + Suspense.
- Render error? → error boundary. Event or async error? → `try/catch` + state.

**Rendering:** trigger → render (pure, may run more than once) → commit (only differences) → paint → layout effects (before paint) / passive effects (after). Same type + position keeps state; a new key or type resets it. Children re-render with their parent by default.

**Rendering strategies:** CSR (empty HTML) · SSR (HTML per request, then hydrate) · SSG (HTML at build) · ISR (static, rebuilt after N seconds) · streaming (shell first, Suspense parts later) · PPR (static shell + streamed dynamic parts) · RSC (server-only components; payload with client references).

**Anti-patterns to name in interviews:** mutating state; index keys on dynamic lists; defining components inside components; derived state synced with effects; effects without cleanup; missing dependencies; giant contexts; `"use client"` everywhere; `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on unsanitised input; testing implementation details.

**Project starter (2026):** Vite + React + TypeScript (or Next.js / React Router framework mode) · React Compiler · ESLint (`eslint-plugin-react-hooks`) or oxlint · Vitest + Testing Library + user-event + MSW · Playwright for E2E · TanStack Query for server state · React Hook Form + Zod for forms · Zustand when you need a store · Tailwind or CSS Modules.

## 75. Most Asked React Theory Questions

**Basics**

1. **What is React, and why use it?** → A library for building UIs from components; you describe the UI for the current state and React updates the DOM efficiently (Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it)).
2. **What is JSX?** → Syntax that compiles to `jsx()` calls creating plain element objects; expressions go in `{}` (Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to)).
3. **Props vs state?** → Props are inputs from the parent, read-only; state is the component's own memory, changed with a setter, causing re-renders (Sections [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components), [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate)).
4. **Why must components be pure?** → React may render them several times or throw renders away; same inputs must give the same output with no side effects (Section [10](#10-keeping-components-pure)).
5. **Why do lists need keys, and why not the index?** → Keys match items between renders; index keys mix up state when items are inserted, removed or reordered (Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys)).
6. **Controlled vs uncontrolled inputs?** → Value in React state with `onChange` vs value kept by the DOM and read on submit (Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs)).

**State and rendering**

7. **Why doesn't state update immediately after `setState`?** → State is a snapshot for the current render; updates are queued and applied in the next render (Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions)).
8. **What is batching?** → Grouping updates into one render; automatic everywhere since React 18 (Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions)).
9. **Why must state be updated immutably?** → React compares with `Object.is`; mutation keeps the same reference, so React skips the update and snapshots get corrupted (Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state)).
10. **What happens when state changes?** → Trigger → render (components called) → commit (DOM differences applied) → paint → effects (Section [15](#15-render-and-commit-what-happens-when-state-changes)).
11. **What is the virtual DOM / reconciliation?** → Element trees compared between renders with two heuristics (type, key) to apply minimal DOM changes (Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch)).
12. **What is Fiber?** → React's architecture since 16: rendering split into units of work that can be paused, prioritised and resumed; commits are atomic (Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering)).
13. **When does a component re-render?** → Its state changes, its parent renders, a context it reads changes, or a subscribed store changes (Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler)).
14. **How do you keep or reset state?** → Same type at the same position keeps it; a different key or type resets it (Section [24](#24-preserving-and-resetting-state-tree-position-and-keys)).
15. **Lifting state up?** → Moving shared state to the closest common parent and passing it down with callbacks (Section [23](#23-sharing-state-lifting-state-up-and-a-single-source-of-truth)).

**Hooks**

16. **What are the Rules of Hooks, and why?** → Call hooks only at the top level of components/custom hooks; React matches hooks to their stored state by call order (Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks)).
17. **`useEffect` vs `useLayoutEffect`?** → After paint vs before paint (synchronously after commit); layout effects are for measuring and adjusting (Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop)).
18. **What is the dependency array, and what happens if it's wrong?** → Every reactive value the effect reads; missing ones cause stale values, unstable ones cause re-runs every render (Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode)).
19. **Why does my effect run twice in development?** → StrictMode mounts, unmounts and remounts to check your cleanup; production runs once (Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react)).
20. **When don't you need an effect?** → Derived data, user-event logic, resetting state on prop change, notifying parents (Section [32](#32-you-might-not-need-an-effect)).
21. **`useRef` vs `useState`?** → Both persist across renders; only state changes trigger re-renders (Section [28](#28-refs-remembering-values-without-re-rendering)).
22. **`useMemo` vs `useCallback` vs `memo`?** → Cache a value / a function / a component's render; only help when inputs are stable and the work is expensive (Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler)).
23. **What is the React Compiler?** → A build-time tool (1.0 in October 2025) that inserts memoisation automatically for components that follow the Rules of React (Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler)).
24. **What is `useEffectEvent`?** → Extracts non-reactive logic from an effect so it reads the latest props without being a dependency (React 19.2, Section [33](#33-separating-events-from-effects-useeffectevent-and-removing-dependencies)).
25. **How do custom hooks work?** → Functions starting with `use` that call hooks; they share logic, not state (Section [38](#38-custom-hooks-reusing-stateful-logic)).
26. **`useReducer` vs `useState`?** → A reducer centralises complex update logic and is testable on its own (Section [35](#35-usereducer-state-logic-in-one-place)).

**Architecture and data**

27. **Context vs a state library?** → Context passes values down; every reader re-renders on change; stores with selectors re-render only affected components (Sections [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply), [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai)).
28. **How do you avoid prop drilling?** → Composition (pass elements/children) first, then context or a store (Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components)).
29. **How do you fetch data correctly?** → Prefer a data library or framework loaders; by hand: loading/error states and a race guard in the effect cleanup (Sections [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller), [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query)).
30. **What is server state, and why is it different?** → Data owned by a server: cached copies can go stale and need deduplication, refetching and invalidation (Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query)).
31. **What are React 19 actions?** → Async functions passed to `<form action>` or transitions; React tracks pending state, errors and optimistic updates (Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic)).
32. **How do error boundaries work, and what don't they catch?** → Class components that render a fallback for render errors below them; not event handlers or async code (Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors)).
33. **What do Suspense and `lazy` do?** → Show a fallback while code or data loads; `lazy` splits components into separate chunks (Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size)).
34. **What are portals for?** → Rendering into another DOM node (modals) while keeping React context and event bubbling (Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals)).

**Server and modern React**

35. **CSR vs SSR vs SSG vs ISR?** → Browser renders / server per request / build time / static with background regeneration (Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr)).
36. **What is hydration, and what causes mismatches?** → React adopting server HTML on the client; differing first renders (time, random, window checks, invalid nesting) (Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches)).
37. **What is streaming SSR?** → Sending the shell with Suspense fallbacks first and the slow parts later in the same response (Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense)).
38. **Server Components vs Client Components?** → Server-only, async, no client JS vs interactive components marked `"use client"`; the RSC payload carries client references (Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work)).
39. **What are Server Functions, and what must you remember about them?** → Server code callable from the client by reference; each is a public endpoint needing authentication and validation (Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work)).
40. **How does caching work in Next.js 16?** → Cache Components: dynamic by default, opt in with `"use cache"`, `cacheLife`, `cacheTag`, expire with `updateTag`/`revalidateTag` (Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching)).
41. **`useTransition` vs `useDeferredValue`?** → Mark updates you trigger as non-urgent vs defer a value you receive (Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition)).
42. **What do `Activity` and `ViewTransition` do?** → Hide UI while keeping state (19.2) / animate transition updates with the View Transitions API (19.3) (Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition)).
43. **How would you build a streaming AI chat UI?** → POST to your server route, read the streamed response chunk by chunk, append tokens with updaters, support Stop with `AbortController` (Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat)).

**Production and practice**

44. **How do you test React components?** → Render, interact like a user (user-event), assert on what's visible with role-based queries; mock the network with MSW; a few E2E tests (Sections [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event), [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end)).
45. **How do you find and fix a slow component?** → Profile; move state down / lift content up; memoise or enable the Compiler; virtualise lists; split code (Sections [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler)–[47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size)).
46. **What are Core Web Vitals?** → LCP (loading), INP (responsiveness), CLS (visual stability), measured from real users (Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment)).
47. **How do you make components accessible?** → Semantic elements, labels, keyboard support, focus management, ARIA only to fill gaps; test with roles and axe (Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals)).
48. **How do you internationalise a React app?** → Translation keys with plural rules, `Intl` formatting, `dir` and logical CSS for RTL (Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts)).
49. **Class components vs function components?** → Lifecycle methods vs hooks; classes remain for error boundaries and legacy code (Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props)).
50. **What changed in React 19 and 19.x?** → Actions and form hooks, `use`, Server Components/Functions stable, `ref` as a prop; then owner stacks, `Activity`, `useEffectEvent`, `ViewTransition`, Fragment refs, `browser()` (Section [69](#69-whats-new-20222026-react-18-to-193-and-the-ecosystem)).

---

## 76. Glossary: Every Term in These Notes

Every technical term from the **Words to know** boxes, A to Z, with a plain definition and a link to the section that teaches it (the first link is where it's introduced). Terms are listed by their main word; symbols and code names (like `useState` or `key`) are sorted by their first letter.


### A

- **`AbortController`:** cancels the in-flight `fetch` in the cleanup (saves bandwidth too); the aborted `fetch` rejects with an `AbortError` that you ignore. *(Section [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller))*
- **`AbortController` / `AbortSignal`:** a way to cancel a `fetch` (or other work): pass `controller.signal`, then call `controller.abort()`. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **`AbortController` for streams:** cancels a streaming fetch (a "Stop generating" button). *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **Abstraction:** hiding details behind a well-named interface; custom hooks let components say *what* they need (`useOnlineStatus()`) instead of *how* to get it. *(Section [38](#38-custom-hooks-reusing-stateful-logic))*
- **Accessibility (a11y):** designing so people with disabilities can perceive, operate and understand the UI ("a11y" = a + 11 letters + y). *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **Accessor hooks:** tiny custom hooks such as `useTasks()` that call `useContext` and throw a helpful error when used outside the provider. *(Section [37](#37-scaling-up-with-reducer-and-context))*
- **Accordion:** a list of panels where opening one panel closes the others. *(Section [23](#23-sharing-state-lifting-state-up-and-a-single-source-of-truth))*
- **`act`:** React's testing helper that runs updates and effects to completion before you look at the page; Testing Library calls it for you. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **Action:** a plain object describing what happened, by convention with a `type` field: `{ type: "deleted", id: 3 }`. *(Section [35](#35-usereducer-state-logic-in-one-place), [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui), [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic))*
- **Action type:** a string naming the event, past tense by convention (`"added"`, `"changed"`), describing what the user did rather than the state change. *(Section [35](#35-usereducer-state-logic-in-one-place))*
- **`<Activity mode="visible" | "hidden">`:** hides its children without unmounting them: state and DOM are kept, effects are cleaned up while hidden and set up again when visible, and hidden content can pre-render at low priority. *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **`actualDuration` / `baseDuration`:** time spent rendering the subtree in this commit / estimated time to render it from scratch without memoisation. *(Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler))*
- **Add / remove / replace / insert:** `[...arr, item]` · `arr.filter(x => x.id !== id)` · `arr.map(x => x.id === id ? newX : x)` · `[...arr.slice(0, i), item, ...arr.slice(i)]` (or `arr.toSpliced(i, 0, item)`). *(Section [18](#18-updating-arrays-in-state))*
- **Adjusting state during render:** for the rare case where some state must change when a prop changes, compare with the previous prop **during render** and set state there (React re-renders immediately, before the commit); a `key` is usually simpler. *(Section [32](#32-you-might-not-need-an-effect))*
- **API (application programming interface):** a defined way for programs to talk; for web apps, usually URLs that return JSON. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **App Router:** Next.js's router based on the `app/` directory and React Server Components (the older `pages/` directory is the **Pages Router**). *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications):** attributes like `aria-label`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-live`, `role="dialog"` that add meaning when HTML can't express it. First rule of ARIA: don't use ARIA if a native element does the job. *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **`aria-live` region:** an element whose changes screen readers announce (toasts, "3 results found"). *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **Array:** an ordered list `[10, 20, 30]`; items are read by **index** from 0: `arr[0]`. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Arrow function:** a shorter function syntax: `(a, b) => a + b`. With braces you need `return`: `(a, b) => { return a + b; }`. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **`as const`:** makes TypeScript keep exact literal values (`["sm", "md"] as const` → a readonly tuple of `"sm" | "md"`). *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **`async` function:** a function that always returns a promise and may use `await` inside. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **Attribute:** extra information on an element, written `name="value"`: `<img src="tea.png" alt="A cup of tea">`. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Auto-scroll:** keeping the newest message in view (a ref + `scrollIntoView` after updates). *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **`await`:** pauses the `async` function until a promise settles, then gives its value (or throws its error) so you can use `try/catch`. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **axe-core:** an open-source engine that tests a page for accessibility violations automatically (it finds a large share of issues, not all). *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*

### B

- **Background refetch:** stale data is shown immediately while a fresh copy loads (stale-while-revalidate). *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **Backpressure / buffering:** handling data that arrives faster than you can process it (batch updates rather than one state update per tiny chunk if needed). *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **Bail out:** if a setter is called with a value equal to the current one (`Object.is`), React may skip re-rendering that component. *(Section [15](#15-render-and-commit-what-happens-when-state-changes))*
- **Bail-out:** skipping work because inputs are unchanged. *(Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler))*
- **Barrel file:** an `index.ts` that re-exports many modules; convenient, but large barrels can slow builds and tests and hurt tree shaking. *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Batching:** grouping multiple state updates into a single re-render. Since React 18 this is **automatic** everywhere: event handlers, timeouts, promises, native listeners. *(Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions), [72](#72-behaviour-questions-what-renders-what-logs-and-when))*
- **Boolean shorthand:** `<Button disabled />` is the same as `disabled={true}`. *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **Breakpoint / `debugger`:** pausing code in the browser's DevTools to inspect variables; the `debugger;` statement pauses there when DevTools is open. *(Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors))*
- **Browser:** the program that downloads and shows web pages (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge). *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **`browser()` (19.3, `react-dom`):** `use(browser())` makes a component render only in the browser: on the server it suspends (the fallback goes into the HTML), on the client it continues. *(Section [69](#69-whats-new-20222026-react-18-to-193-and-the-ecosystem))*
- **Built-in (host) component:** a lowercase tag such as `<div>` or `<button>`, which React turns into a real DOM element. *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*
- **Bundle:** a JavaScript file produced by the build, combining many modules. *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*
- **Bundle analyser:** a tool that shows what's inside each chunk (`rollup-plugin-visualizer`, `vite-bundle-visualizer`, `source-map-explorer`). *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*
- **Bundle size benefit:** libraries used only in Server Components (a markdown parser, a date library, a database client) add **zero** bytes to the client JavaScript. *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **Bundler / build:** combines your many source files and libraries into a few optimised files (`dist/`), transforming TypeScript and JSX into plain JavaScript. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*

### C

- **Cache:** storing previous responses so going back to a screen is instant; hand-written effects have none. *(Section [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller))*
- **Cache Components:** Next.js 16's caching model (enabled with `cacheComponents: true`; default for new apps from 16.4 and planned as the default in Next.js 17): everything is dynamic unless you mark it cached with `"use cache"`; static parts are prerendered as a shell (partial prerendering). *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Call order:** the sequence in which a component calls hooks during render; React matches hook calls to slots purely by position. *(Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks))*
- **Call stack:** the list of functions currently running; JavaScript runs one thing at a time on a single thread. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **Callback:** a function you hand to something else to be called later: `setTimeout(callback, 1000)`. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **Callback prop:** a function passed down so the child can tell the parent something happened: `onAdd`, `onChange`. By convention prop names start with `on` and handler functions with `handle`. *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **camelCase attributes:** event and most multi-word attributes are camelCase in JSX: `onClick`, `tabIndex`, `maxLength`, `autoFocus`. Exceptions: `aria-*` and `data-*` keep their dashes. *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **Canary / experimental channel:** React's pre-release builds where new APIs appear before becoming stable. *(Section [69](#69-whats-new-20222026-react-18-to-193-and-the-ecosystem))*
- **Capture phase (`onClickCapture`):** handlers ending in `Capture` run on the way **down**, before the target's own handler. *(Section [13](#13-responding-to-events))*
- **Cascading render:** a parent's render re-rendering its whole subtree by default. *(Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler))*
- **CDN (content delivery network):** servers around the world that cache and serve static files close to users. *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **Chain of effects:** effects that set state that triggers other effects; hard to follow, many extra renders. *(Section [32](#32-you-might-not-need-an-effect))*
- **`children`:** the special prop holding whatever is written between an element's opening and closing tags. *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to), [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components))*
- **`children` prop:** whatever is nested between a component's tags: in `<Card><p>Hi</p></Card>`, `Card` receives the `p` as `children` (more in Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components)). *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **Chunk:** one of several bundle files; the **entry chunk** loads first, others load later. *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*
- **Chunked transfer encoding:** the HTTP mechanism that lets a server send a response in pieces without knowing its total length. *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **Class / id:** a **class** (`class="price"`) labels any number of elements for styling; an **id** (`id="cart"`) names exactly one element. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Class component:** the older way to write components with `class X extends Component` and `render()` (Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props)); error boundaries are the one thing still requiring a class (libraries wrap it for you). *(Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors), [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*
- **`className`:** the JSX prop for the HTML `class` attribute; a string of space-separated class names. *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js))*
- **`className` / `htmlFor`:** JSX names for HTML's `class` and `for`, because `class` and `for` are reserved words in JavaScript. *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **Cleanup function:** undoes the setup (disconnect, unsubscribe, clear a timer); runs before the next setup and on unmount. *(Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react))*
- **Client Component:** a component in a file starting with `"use client"` (and everything it imports); rendered on the server for the first HTML, then hydrated and interactive in the browser. *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **Client reference:** an entry such as `I[69819,["…chunk.js"],"LikeButton"]`: "load this module from these chunks and use its `LikeButton` export here". *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **Client-side routing:** changing what's shown when the URL changes, in JavaScript, without asking the server for a new HTML page. *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **Client-side validation:** checking input in the browser for fast feedback (`required`, `pattern`, or code); the server must validate again because users can bypass the browser. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **Closest common parent (owner):** the nearest ancestor of every component that reads a piece of state; that's where the state should live. *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **Closure:** a function that remembers variables from where it was created; the setter closes over its slot index. *(Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks), [70](#70-interview-coding-hooks-and-utilities-from-scratch))*
- **`clsx` / `classnames`:** tiny helpers that join class names conditionally: `clsx("card", soldOut && "card--soldout")`. *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js))*
- **Codemod:** a script that rewrites code automatically for an upgrade (`npx codemod react/19/migration-recipe`, `npx @next/codemod upgrade`). *(Section [69](#69-whats-new-20222026-react-18-to-193-and-the-ecosystem))*
- **Coercion (`z.coerce.number()`):** converting input strings ("2") to the right type before validating; form fields are always strings. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **Colocation:** keeping the reducer, contexts, provider and hooks in one file (`TasksContext.tsx`). *(Section [37](#37-scaling-up-with-reducer-and-context), [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Combobox pattern:** the accessible autocomplete: an input with `role="combobox"`, a `listbox` of `option`s, `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant` for the highlighted option. *(Section [71](#71-machine-coding-round-classic-components-built-and-tested))*
- **Commit:** applying the computed changes to the DOM (insert, update, remove nodes) in one go. *(Section [15](#15-render-and-commit-what-happens-when-state-changes))*
- **Commit phase is synchronous:** once React starts applying DOM changes it finishes in one go; only the render phase is interruptible. *(Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*
- **Compiler / transpiler:** a tool that rewrites code into another form; esbuild, SWC, Babel and TypeScript all compile JSX into function calls. *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **Component:** a reusable piece of UI, such as a button, a product card or a whole checkout page, written as a JavaScript function. *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **Component hierarchy:** the tree of components you draw on the mockup: `FilterableProductTable` → `SearchBar` + `ProductTable` → `ProductCategoryRow` + `ProductRow`. *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **Component stack:** the list of components from the root to where an error happened, printed under React's error messages. *(Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors))*
- **Component tree:** the nesting of components: `App` renders `Header` and `ProductCard`, and so on down to plain HTML elements. *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*
- **`ComponentProps<"button">`:** all the props a `<button>` accepts; used to make wrapper components that pass everything through. *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **Composition:** building complex components by combining simpler ones, passing components and elements into each other. *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components))*
- **Composition rule:** Server Components can render Client Components and pass Server Components to them as `children`; Client Components can't import Server Components (but can receive them as props). *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **Computed property name (`[name]: value`):** uses a variable as the key: `{ ...form, [e.target.name]: e.target.value }`. *(Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state))*
- **Concurrent rendering:** rendering that can be interrupted, restarted or abandoned; enabled for updates marked as transitions (`startTransition`) and deferred values. *(Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*
- **Conditional rendering:** showing different UI depending on conditions. *(Section [11](#11-conditional-rendering))*
- **Conditional variable:** assigning JSX to a variable with `if`/`else` above the return, then using `{content}`. *(Section [11](#11-conditional-rendering))*
- **`connection()`:** marks the rest of a component as request-time (dynamic) rendering. *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **`constructor(props)`:** initialises state (`this.state = {…}`); must call `super(props)`. *(Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*
- **Container / layout component:** a component whose job is arrangement and styling (a card frame, a two-column page) and which renders `children` inside. *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components))*
- **Content hashing / immutable caching:** file names like `index-Cl6Bt99l.js` change when content changes, so they can be served with `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable`; `index.html` must not be cached long. *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **Context:** a way to pass a value deep down the tree without props, created with `createContext(defaultValue)`. *(Section [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply))*
- **Context splitting:** using several smaller contexts (e.g. state and dispatch, or user and theme) so a change only re-renders the components that read that part. *(Section [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply))*
- **Contract test:** checking that the mock and the real API agree (e.g. validating both against the same Zod schema or OpenAPI spec). *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **Contradictory state:** two pieces of state that can disagree (`isSending` and `isSent` both true). *(Section [22](#22-choosing-the-state-structure))*
- **Controlled component:** an input whose displayed value is set from props or state (`value`/`checked`) and changed only through `onChange`. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **Controlled component (general sense):** a component whose important information is driven by **props** from its parent (like `<Panel isActive={…} />`); the parent controls it. *(Section [23](#23-sharing-state-lifting-state-up-and-a-single-source-of-truth))*
- **Core Web Vitals:** Google's user-experience metrics: **LCP** (largest contentful paint: main content visible; good ≤ 2.5 s), **INP** (interaction to next paint: responsiveness; good ≤ 200 ms), **CLS** (cumulative layout shift: unexpected movement; good ≤ 0.1). *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **`createBrowserRouter` / `createMemoryRouter` + `RouterProvider`:** create a data router using the real browser URL / an in-memory history (for tests and these examples). *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **CSR (client-side rendering):** the browser downloads JavaScript and renders everything; the initial HTML is just `<div id="root"></div>`. *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **CSS (Cascading Style Sheets):** rules that style elements: `.price { color: green; }`. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **CSS custom properties (CSS variables):** `--accent: #16a34a;` defined once and used as `var(--accent)`; change one variable to re-theme everything (dark mode). *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js))*
- **CSS Modules:** files named `*.module.css`; the build tool renames each class to something unique (`_title_x1y2z`) and gives you an object mapping your names to the real ones: `styles.title`. *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js))*
- **CSS-in-JS:** writing styles in JavaScript (styled-components, Emotion); runtime versions inject `<style>` tags while the app runs, which costs performance and works poorly with Server Components, so **zero-runtime** tools (vanilla-extract, Panda CSS, StyleX) extract static CSS at build time instead. *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js))*
- **Cursor (hook index):** the counter React advances on each hook call during a render. *(Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks))*
- **Cursor-based pagination:** asking for "the 20 items after this id" instead of "page 3"; stable when items are inserted (Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query) loads pages this way). *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **Custom hook:** a JavaScript function whose name starts with `use` and that calls other hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, other custom hooks). *(Section [38](#38-custom-hooks-reusing-stateful-logic))*

### D

- **`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`:** the deliberately scary escape hatch that inserts raw HTML; only for trusted or sanitised HTML (`javascript.md`, [Frontend Security](javascript.md#35-frontend-security-xss-csrf-csp-prototype-pollution-and-the-supply-chain)). *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **Debounce:** wait until a value has stopped changing for some time before using it. *(Section [38](#38-custom-hooks-reusing-stateful-logic), [70](#70-interview-coding-hooks-and-utilities-from-scratch))*
- **Declarative:** code that says **what** the result should be: "the list shows one `li` per item". *(Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it))*
- **Declarative UI states:** you describe what each state looks like; React handles moving between the pictures. *(Section [21](#21-reacting-to-input-with-state-ui-as-a-state-machine))*
- **Deduplication:** many components asking for the same key at once share **one** request. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **Default action / `preventDefault()`:** what the browser does on its own after an event (a form submit reloads the page, a link navigates); `event.preventDefault()` cancels it. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Default export / named export:** a file's one main export (`export default function App`) vs extra ones (`export function Button`); you can use either for components (Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules)). *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*
- **Default prop value:** a fallback in the destructuring: `function Avatar({ size = 48 })`. *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **Default value:** a fallback used when a value is `undefined`: `function f({ size = "md" }) {}`. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules), [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply))*
- **Dependency / devDependency:** a package the app needs at runtime (React) / a package only needed while developing or building (Vite, TypeScript, test tools). *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **Dependency array:** the list of reactive values the effect uses. `[a, b]`: re-run when `a` or `b` changes (compared with `Object.is`); `[]`: run only after the first render (and clean up on unmount); **no array**: re-run after every render. *(Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react))*
- **Dependency direction:** shared code must not import from features, and features shouldn't import each other's internals; tools like ESLint's `import/no-restricted-paths` or dependency-cruiser enforce it. *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Deprecation:** marking an API as discouraged before removing it (Create React App in February 2025; `forwardRef` is no longer needed in React 19). *(Section [69](#69-whats-new-20222026-react-18-to-193-and-the-ecosystem))*
- **Derived (computed) value:** a value calculated from props or state during render (a filtered list, a total); it is **not** state. *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **Derived state anti-pattern:** storing a value computed from other state (`fullName`, `visibleTodos`) and updating it in an effect; it costs an extra render and can show stale data for one frame. *(Section [32](#32-you-might-not-need-an-effect))*
- **Design system:** a shared set of design decisions (tokens) and components (Button, Input, Dialog) with documentation, used across products. *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Design tokens:** named values for colours, spacing and fonts shared by a design system (often as CSS variables). *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js), [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Destructuring:** unpacking values into variables: `const { name, price } = item;` and `const [first, second] = list;`. React props and `useState` both use it. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Dev server:** a local web server (`http://localhost:5173`) that serves your app while you develop. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **Development double-run:** StrictMode's mount → unmount → mount check; it only happens in development and only on mount. *(Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode))*
- **Development vs production React:** development builds include warnings, StrictMode double calls and debugging helpers; production builds remove them and are smaller and faster. *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **`<dialog>` element:** the native HTML modal, with `showModal()` providing focus handling, Esc to close and an inert background in browsers. *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **Different-type rule:** a different `type` at a position means React destroys the old subtree (DOM and state) and builds the new one. *(Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch))*
- **Dirty / touched:** a field whose value changed from its default / that the user has focused and left. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **Discriminated union:** a union of object types that share a tag field (`status`), so checking the tag tells TypeScript which other fields exist. *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **Discriminated union of actions (TypeScript):** `type Action = { type: "added"; text: string } | { type: "deleted"; id: number }`, so each case knows its fields. *(Section [35](#35-usereducer-state-logic-in-one-place))*
- **Dispatch:** sending an action to the reducer: `dispatch({ type: "deleted", id: 3 })`. *(Section [35](#35-usereducer-state-logic-in-one-place))*
- **`document`:** the JavaScript object that represents the whole page; `document.body` is the `<body>` element. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **DOM (Document Object Model):** the tree of JavaScript objects the browser builds from HTML; JavaScript reads and changes the page through it. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **DOM ref:** a ref whose `current` React sets to a DOM node: `<input ref={inputRef} />`. It's `null` before the commit and after the node is removed. *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **Double buffering (current vs work-in-progress tree):** React renders into a copy of the tree and swaps it in on commit; the screen always shows a complete tree. *(Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*
- **Duplicated state:** the same data stored twice (the list of items **and** a copy of the selected item); edits to one don't reach the other. *(Section [22](#22-choosing-the-state-structure))*
- **Dynamic `import()`:** a function-style import that loads a module **at runtime** and returns a promise; bundlers turn each one into a separate chunk. *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*

### E

- **`e.target.value` / `e.target.checked`:** the current text of an input / whether a checkbox is ticked. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **Early return:** `if (!user) return <Login />;` at the top of a component; the rest of the function handles the normal case. *(Section [11](#11-conditional-rendering))*
- **Ecosystem:** the libraries, tools, frameworks, tutorials and jobs around a technology; React's is the largest of any UI library. *(Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it))*
- **Edge cases:** empty input, no results, slow and out-of-order responses, very long lists, rapid clicks. *(Section [71](#71-machine-coding-round-classic-components-built-and-tested))*
- **Effect:** a function React runs after the commit (and normally after the browser paints) to synchronise with an external system. *(Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react))*
- **Effect event:** the function returned by `useEffectEvent`; don't pass it to other components or call it during render. *(Section [33](#33-separating-events-from-effects-useeffectevent-and-removing-dependencies))*
- **Effect lifecycle:** an effect's own cycle: start syncing → (deps change) stop → start with new values → … → stop on unmount. *(Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode))*
- **End-to-end (E2E) test:** a test of the whole running app in a real browser, as a user would use it. *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **Entry point:** the first file that runs (`src/main.tsx`), which starts the app. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **Error boundary:** a component implementing `static getDerivedStateFromError` (to switch to fallback UI) and/or `componentDidCatch` (to log); catches errors thrown during rendering, in lifecycle methods and in constructors below it. *(Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors))*
- **Error monitoring:** capturing errors in production (`window.onerror`, `unhandledrejection`, React's root error callbacks) and sending them to a service such as Sentry or Datadog, grouped and with source maps. *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **Error state:** what the UI shows when the request failed, often with a retry. *(Section [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller))*
- **Escape hatch:** a feature for stepping outside React's normal data flow (refs, effects); useful, but use sparingly. *(Section [28](#28-refs-remembering-values-without-re-rendering))*
- **Escaping:** turning special characters into safe text (`<` → `&lt;`), so text from users can never become markup. JSX escapes everything in `{}` automatically. *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **Event:** something that happened that code can react to: a click, a key press, a form submit, the page finishing loading. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Event bubbling:** after an event fires on the clicked element, it travels **up** through each ancestor, so a listener on a parent also hears clicks on its children. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Event delegation:** attaching one listener high in the tree instead of one per element; React attaches its listeners once to the **root container** and works out which components' handlers to call. *(Section [13](#13-responding-to-events))*
- **Event handler:** a function passed as an `on…` prop (`onClick`, `onChange`, `onSubmit`, `onKeyDown`) that React calls when that event fires. *(Section [13](#13-responding-to-events))*
- **Event handler prop (custom):** your own components can accept handler props with any name starting with `on`: `<Toolbar onPlay={...} />`; the name is your API. *(Section [13](#13-responding-to-events))*
- **Event listener (handler):** a function the browser calls when an event happens: `button.addEventListener("click", fn)`. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Event loop:** the mechanism that, whenever the call stack is empty, picks the next waiting callback and runs it. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **Event types:** `React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>`, `React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>`, `React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>`, `React.KeyboardEvent`: the type of `e` in handlers (inferred automatically when the handler is written inline). *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **Event-specific logic:** code that should run because the user **did something** (bought a product, submitted a form); it belongs in that event's handler. *(Section [32](#32-you-might-not-need-an-effect))*
- **`event.target` vs `event.currentTarget`:** `target` is the element where the event started; `currentTarget` is the element whose listener is running right now. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Exhaustive check:** a `default` branch that TypeScript proves unreachable (`const never: never = action`), so adding a new action type without handling it is a compile error. *(Section [35](#35-usereducer-state-logic-in-one-place))*
- **`exhaustive-deps` lint rule:** part of `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`; warns when an effect reads a reactive value that isn't in its dependency array. *(Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode))*
- **Expression vs statement:** an **expression** produces a value (`price * qty`, `a ? b : c`, `items.map(...)`) and can go inside `{}`; a **statement** does something (`if`, `for`, `const x = 1`) and cannot. *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **External store:** data outside React state: a browser API (`navigator.onLine`, `matchMedia`), a third-party store, a module-level variable with listeners. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **External system:** anything React doesn't control: the network, browser APIs (`document.title`, `localStorage`, timers, `window` events), third-party widgets, WebSockets. *(Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react))*

### F

- **Fallback UI:** what the boundary shows instead of the crashed subtree ("Something went wrong. Try again"). *(Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors))*
- **FCP / LCP (first / largest contentful paint):** when the first content / the main content appears on screen (Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment)). *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **FCP / TTFB:** first contentful paint / time to first byte, supporting metrics. *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **Feature flag:** turning features on or off at runtime without redeploying, useful for gradual rollouts. *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **`fetch`:** the built-in function for HTTP requests; returns a promise of a **Response**. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **Fiber:** React's internal object for one component instance; it stores that component's hook list (Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering)). *(Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks), [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*
- **`filter` then `map`:** the usual way to show part of a list: `items.filter(i => i.veg).map(i => <li key={i.id}>…)`. *(Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys))*
- **Fixed vs dynamic row height:** fixed heights make the maths simple; variable heights need measuring each row after it renders. *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **Flaky test:** a test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without code changes, usually from timing or shared state. *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **`flushSync`:** a rarely needed function from `react-dom` that forces React to apply an update and update the DOM **immediately**, bypassing batching (e.g. to scroll to a just-added item). *(Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions))*
- **`flushSync` + scroll:** to scroll to an item added by a state update, apply the update synchronously first (Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions)), then scroll. *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **Focus management:** moving focus deliberately (into an opened modal, to an error summary) and returning it when content closes. *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **Focus trap:** keeping Tab inside an open modal so keyboard users don't wander behind it. *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **`focus()` / `select()` / `blur()`:** DOM methods that move keyboard focus to an element / select its text / remove focus. *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **`<form action={fn}>`:** React calls `fn(formData)` on submit, prevents the page reload, and resets uncontrolled fields after it succeeds. *(Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic))*
- **Form reset:** after a successful action React resets the form's uncontrolled inputs, like a browser does after a normal submit. *(Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic))*
- **`<Form>`:** React Router's form; submits to the route's action without a page reload (and works as a normal HTML form before JavaScript loads in framework mode). *(Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui))*
- **`formAction`:** the same, on a specific submit button (`<button formAction={save}>`). *(Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic))*
- **`FormData`:** a built-in object that reads every named field of a `<form>`: `new FormData(form).get("email")`; `Object.fromEntries(formData)` turns it into a plain object. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **`forwardRef` (legacy):** the pre-19 way to accept a ref in a function component; React 19 passes `ref` as a normal prop. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **Fragment (`<>…</>` or `<Fragment>`):** groups several elements without adding a wrapper to the DOM. Use `<Fragment key={…}>` when it needs a key (Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys)). *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **Fragment ref (19.3):** `<Fragment ref={ref}>` gives a `FragmentInstance` with event, focus, observer and measurement methods that act on the fragment's DOM children. *(Section [69](#69-whats-new-20222026-react-18-to-193-and-the-ecosystem))*
- **`Fragment` with a key:** `<Fragment key={id}>…</Fragment>` when each item renders several siblings. *(Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys))*
- **Frontend / backend:** the **frontend** is the part of an app that runs in the user's browser (the UI); the **backend** runs on servers (databases, business logic, APIs). *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **Full-stack developer:** someone who builds both the frontend and the backend. *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **Function / parameter / argument / return value:** a reusable block of code; **parameters** are the names in its definition, **arguments** the values passed in a call, and the **return value** what it hands back. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Function component:** a function that returns JSX (or `null`); the only kind of component new code uses (older **class components** are covered in Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props)). *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*

### G

- **`gcTime`:** how long unused cache entries are kept (default 5 minutes) before being garbage collected. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **Generic (`<T>`):** a type parameter, a "type variable" filled in at use: `useState<string | null>(null)`, `List<T>`. *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **`getBoundingClientRect()`:** returns an element's size and position on screen (needs a real layout engine). *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **Global (client) state:** UI data shared across distant components and owned by the browser, not by a server. *(Section [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **Global CSS:** a normal stylesheet whose class names apply everywhere; two components using `.title` clash. *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js))*
- **Granularity:** how much UI one boundary protects: one for the whole app, one per route, one per widget. *(Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors))*
- **Grouping by type vs by feature:** `components/`, `hooks/`, `services/` folders for the whole app vs one folder per feature (`features/cart/`) containing everything it needs. *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **gzip / Brotli:** compression applied by servers; transfer size is the compressed size. *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*

### H

- **`handle…` / `on…` naming:** props are named `onSomething`; the functions you pass are usually named `handleSomething`. *(Section [13](#13-responding-to-events))*
- **Headless component library:** unstyled components that provide behaviour and accessibility (Radix UI, React Aria, Base UI), styled by your design system; shadcn/ui copies such components into your repo. *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Heuristic:** a rule of thumb that gives a good-enough answer fast instead of the perfect answer slowly. A perfect tree diff is O(n³); React's heuristics make it O(n) (one pass, proportional to the number of elements). *(Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch))*
- **Higher-order component (HOC):** a function that takes a component and returns a new one with extra props or behaviour (`withRouter(Component)`, `connect(...)(Component)`). *(Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*
- **"Highlight updates":** a DevTools option that flashes components as they re-render. *(Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors))*
- **History API:** browser functions (`history.pushState`, the `popstate` event) that change the URL and track back/forward without a reload. *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **Hook:** a special function whose name starts with `use` (`useState`, `useEffect`…) that lets a component "hook into" React features. Hooks may only be called at the top level of a component or another hook (Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks)). *(Section [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate))*
- **Hook API design:** what the hook returns: a value (`isOnline`), a tuple (`[value, setValue]` like `useState`) or an object (`{ data, error, status }`). *(Section [38](#38-custom-hooks-reusing-stateful-logic))*
- **Hook slot (memoized state):** one entry in a component's list of hook data (a state value, an effect's deps, a ref object). *(Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks))*
- **Hot module replacement (HMR) / Fast Refresh:** when you save a file, only that module is swapped in the running page, and React keeps component state. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **HTML (HyperText Markup Language):** the text format that describes a page's content and structure: `<h1>Menu</h1><button>Order</button>`. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **HTTP request / response / status code:** a request asks a server for something (`GET /api/menu`); the response carries a status code (`200` OK, `404` Not Found, `500` Server Error) and a body. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **`hydrateRoot(container, <App />)`:** React DOM's client API for hydration (instead of `createRoot`). *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*
- **Hydration:** making server-rendered HTML interactive by running React on the client and adopting the existing DOM. *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*
- **Hydration mismatch:** the client's first render differs from the server HTML; React logs it, discards the server HTML for that subtree (up to the nearest Suspense boundary) and renders it on the client, which is slower and can flicker. *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*

### I

- **i18next / react-i18next:** a popular i18n library and its React binding (`useTranslation()` returns a `t` function). *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **ICU message format:** a standard syntax for messages with plurals and selections (`{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}`), used by FormatJS/react-intl. *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Idempotent:** doing it twice has the same result as doing it once; pure rendering is idempotent. *(Section [10](#10-keeping-components-pure))*
- **`ignore` flag:** a local variable set to `true` in the cleanup; the response handler checks it and drops results from an effect that has since been cleaned up. *(Section [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller))*
- **Immer / `produce` / `useImmer`:** a small library: inside `produce(state, draft => { draft.address.city = "Pune"; })` you "mutate" a **draft**, and Immer returns a new object with only the changed parts copied (structural sharing). `useImmer` is a `useState` replacement built on it. *(Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state))*
- **Immutability:** the habit of never changing existing data, only making changed copies. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Immutable update:** building a new object that includes the change and leaves the original untouched. *(Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state))*
- **Imperative:** code that says **how**, step by step: "create an `li`, set its text, append it". *(Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it))*
- **Implementation detail:** something users can't see (state variables, component names, CSS classes); tests shouldn't depend on it. *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **Impossible state:** a combination of separate booleans that should never happen (`isLoading && isError`), which separate flags allow and a single status variable prevents. *(Section [21](#21-reacting-to-input-with-state-ui-as-a-state-machine))*
- **`&&` in JSX:** `{isNew && <Badge />}` shows the badge when `isNew` is truthy, otherwise renders the left value (`false` renders nothing). *(Section [11](#11-conditional-rendering))*
- **Index key:** using the array position (`key={index}`) as the key; fine for static lists that never reorder, wrong when items are inserted, removed or reordered. *(Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys))*
- **Index route:** the child shown at the parent's exact path (`/teas` itself, not `/teas/7`). *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **Infinite scroll:** loading the next page automatically when a sentinel element near the end becomes visible, detected with `IntersectionObserver`. *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **Inheritance:** making a class from another class; React apps essentially never use it for components; composition covers every case. *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components))*
- **Initial render vs re-render:** the first render creates all DOM nodes; re-renders only update what changed. *(Section [15](#15-render-and-commit-what-happens-when-state-changes))*
- **Initial value:** used only on the **first** render; later renders ignore the argument. *(Section [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate))*
- **Inline handler:** a handler written directly in JSX: `onClick={() => setOpen(true)}`. *(Section [13](#13-responding-to-events))*
- **Inline styles (`style={{…}}`):** fine for truly dynamic values (a progress bar's width), poor for everything else (no hover states, media queries or reuse). *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js))*
- **INP (Interaction to Next Paint):** a web performance metric: how long after an interaction the next frame is painted; slow renders hurt it (Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment)). *(Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler))*
- **Internationalisation (i18n) / localisation (l10n):** making software adaptable to languages and regions / adapting it to one ("i18n" = i + 18 letters + n). *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Interpolation:** inserting values into a message: `"Hello, {{name}}"`. *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Interval / timeout id:** the number `setInterval`/`setTimeout` return; needed later to cancel with `clearInterval`/`clearTimeout`. *(Section [28](#28-refs-remembering-values-without-re-rendering))*
- **`Intl` APIs:** built-in JavaScript formatters: `NumberFormat` (numbers, currencies, percentages), `DateTimeFormat` (dates and times, with time zones), `RelativeTimeFormat` ("3 days ago"), `ListFormat` ("tea, coffee and juice"), `PluralRules`, `Collator` (locale-aware sorting). *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Invalidation (`queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey })`):** marks matching queries stale and refetches active ones, typically after a mutation. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **Inverse data flow:** children changing parent-owned state by calling callbacks passed down as props. *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **ISR (incremental static regeneration):** serving a cached static page and regenerating it after `revalidate` seconds; the first visitor after it expires still gets the old page while a fresh one is built (stale-while-revalidate). *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **Issue:** one validation problem, with a `path` (which field) and a `message`. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*

### J

- **Jotai:** "atomic" state: small independent pieces (`atom(0)`), derived atoms (`atom((get) => get(a) * 2)`), read with `useAtom`/`useAtomValue`. *(Section [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **jsdom:** a JavaScript implementation of the browser DOM that runs in Node; tests and these notes render React into it. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **JSON (JavaScript Object Notation):** the text format APIs use for data: `{"name":"Chai","price":180}`. `JSON.parse` turns text into objects; `JSON.stringify` the reverse; `response.json()` reads and parses a response body. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **JSON data:** product lists and other data usually arrive from an API as JSON arrays of objects; components render them. *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **JSX:** the HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript (`<h1>Hi</h1>`) that describes UI; Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to) shows what it turns into. *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*
- **JSX (JavaScript XML):** a syntax extension that lets you write markup in JavaScript; it is not valid JavaScript until a compiler transforms it. *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **`jsx()` / `jsxs()` (the automatic runtime):** the functions JSX compiles into, imported automatically from `react/jsx-runtime` (`jsxs` is used when there are several static children). Older setups compiled to `React.createElement`, which is why old files start with `import React from "react"`. *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*

### K

- **`key`:** a special attribute that identifies an element among its siblings. It is not passed to your component as a prop (read `item.id` separately if you need it). *(Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys))*
- **`key` outside lists:** any component can take a key; changing it tells React "this is a different instance", so it resets. *(Section [24](#24-preserving-and-resetting-state-tree-position-and-keys))*
- **Keyboard operability:** everything clickable must be reachable with Tab and activated with Enter/Space; focus must be visible. *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **Keyed children:** children with keys are matched by key, so reordering moves existing nodes and keeps their state. *(Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch))*

### L

- **Lanes (priorities):** React's way of labelling updates: discrete events like clicks and typing are synchronous/urgent; transitions are low priority and interruptible. *(Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*
- **Latest-value ref:** a ref updated every render so a long-lived callback (an interval) can read current props without being re-created. *(Section [70](#70-interview-coding-hooks-and-utilities-from-scratch))*
- **Layout engine:** the part of a browser that computes sizes and positions; **jsdom doesn't have one**, so measuring and scrolling can't be shown for real in these Node examples. *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **Layout shift / flicker:** a visible jump when something renders in one position and then moves. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **`layout.tsx`:** wraps the pages below it; preserved across navigations (state and DOM stay). *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Lazy initializer:** `useState(() => expensiveSetup())`: pass a **function** so the expensive setup runs only on the first render, not every render. *(Section [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate))*
- **`lazy(load)`:** wraps a dynamic import into a component; React calls `load()` the first time it renders and **suspends** until the module arrives. *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*
- **Leading / trailing call:** whether a throttled or debounced function fires at the start of a burst, at the end, or both. *(Section [70](#70-interview-coding-hooks-and-utilities-from-scratch))*
- **Library vs framework:** a **library** is code you call when you need it (React renders UI; you pick the rest); a **framework** calls *your* code and decides the structure of the whole app (Next.js decides routing, data loading and the server for you). *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **Lifecycle methods:** `componentDidMount` (after the first commit), `componentDidUpdate(prevProps, prevState)` (after each update), `componentWillUnmount` (before removal), `shouldComponentUpdate(nextProps, nextState)` (return `false` to skip a render), `getDerivedStateFromProps` (static, sync state to props), `getSnapshotBeforeUpdate`, plus `componentDidCatch`/`getDerivedStateFromError` (Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors)). *(Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*
- **Lifting content up (children pattern):** passing expensive parts as `children` from above, so a stateful wrapper re-rendering doesn't re-render them (they were created by the parent, whose render didn't happen). *(Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler))*
- **Lifting state up:** moving state from children to a common parent so they can share and coordinate it. *(Section [23](#23-sharing-state-lifting-state-up-and-a-single-source-of-truth))*
- **`<Link to>` / `<NavLink>`:** links that navigate client-side; `NavLink` knows whether it's active (to style the current page). *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **Linter (oxlint / ESLint):** a tool that reads code and warns about likely bugs and style problems; the React Hooks lint rules catch many React mistakes (Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks)). *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **List rendering:** producing one element per array item, usually with `items.map(item => <Row … />)`. *(Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys))*
- **Literal type:** an exact value used as a type: `"success"`. *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **Loader:** `loader({ params, request })` runs before the route renders; its return value is read with `useLoaderData()`. *(Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui))*
- **Loading state:** what the UI shows while waiting (`status: "loading"`). *(Section [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller))*
- **`loading.tsx` / `error.tsx` / `not-found.tsx`:** automatic Suspense fallback / error boundary (a Client Component) / 404 UI for a segment. *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Local / isolated state:** each rendered instance of a component has independent state; two `<Counter />`s count separately. *(Section [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate))*
- **Local mutation:** changing a variable or array **you created during this render**: perfectly fine (`const rows = []; rows.push(...)`). *(Section [10](#10-keeping-components-pure))*
- **Locale:** a language plus regional conventions, written as a tag like `en-IN` (English, India), `hi-IN` (Hindi, India), `ar-EG` (Arabic, Egypt). *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Locator:** Playwright's way to find elements (`page.getByRole("button", { name: "Add" })`), re-evaluated each time it's used. *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **Lock file (`package-lock.json`):** records the exact version of every installed package so every machine installs the same ones. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **Logical AND (`&&`) / nullish coalescing (`??`) / optional chaining (`?.`):** `a && b` gives `b` when `a` is truthy, else `a`; `a ?? b` gives `b` only when `a` is `null` or `undefined`; `user?.address?.city` gives `undefined` instead of crashing when something along the way is missing. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Logical CSS properties:** `margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`, `inset-inline-start` instead of left/right, so layouts flip automatically for RTL. *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Lookup object:** mapping a status to UI with an object (`const icons = { paid: "✅", failed: "❌" }`) instead of a chain of ternaries. *(Section [11](#11-conditional-rendering))*

### M

- **Machine-coding round:** a timed practical interview where you build a UI feature end to end. *(Section [71](#71-machine-coding-round-classic-components-built-and-tested))*
- **Major / minor / patch release:** in semantic versioning, a major release may break things (18 → 19), a minor adds features (19.2 → 19.3), a patch fixes bugs (19.3.0 → 19.3.1). *(Section [69](#69-whats-new-20222026-react-18-to-193-and-the-ecosystem))*
- **`map` / `filter` / `find` / `some` / `reduce`:** array methods that return a **new** array of transformed items / a new array of items that pass a test / the first item that passes / whether any passes / one value accumulated from all items. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Matcher:** an assertion method: `toBe`, `toEqual`, `toHaveTextContent`, `toBeDisabled`… The DOM-specific ones come from `@testing-library/jest-dom`. *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **Memo cache (`_c(n)`):** the per-component array the compiled code uses to store cached values (from `react/compiler-runtime`). *(Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler))*
