- **`memo(Component, arePropsEqual?)`:** returns a component that skips rendering when every prop is `Object.is`-equal to the previous render's (or when your comparison function says so). *(Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler))*
- **Memoisation:** caching a function's result for given inputs to avoid recomputing it. *(Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler))*
- **Memoisation (`useMemo`):** caching an expensive calculation between renders, recomputing only when its inputs change (Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler)). *(Section [32](#32-you-might-not-need-an-effect))*
- **Memoize:** cache a function's results by its arguments. *(Section [70](#70-interview-coding-hooks-and-utilities-from-scratch))*
- **Method binding:** class methods lose `this` when passed as callbacks; bind in the constructor or use arrow-function class fields. *(Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*
- **Middleware (React Router 8):** functions that run before loaders/actions (authentication, logging), always enabled in v8. *(Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui))*
- **Minification:** shortening code (renaming variables, removing whitespace) to reduce size. *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **Minimal reproduction:** the smallest code that still shows the bug; building one finds most bugs by itself. *(Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors))*
- **Minimal state (DRY):** the smallest set of values that must be remembered; everything else is computed when rendering (Don't Repeat Yourself). *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **Mirroring props in state:** `useState(props.color)` copies a prop once and then ignores changes; only do it on purpose (name it `initialColor`). *(Section [22](#22-choosing-the-state-structure))*
- **Missing-key warning:** in development React logs "Each child in a list should have a unique key prop" when keys are missing. *(Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys))*
- **Mock function (`vi.fn()`):** a fake function that records how it was called. *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **Mocking the network:** replacing real HTTP responses with predefined ones in tests (fast, deterministic, no real backend). *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **Mockup:** a picture of the intended screen, from a designer (Figma) or a sketch. *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **Module / `import` / `export`:** each file is a module; `export` makes a value available, `import` brings it into another file. A file has at most one **default export** (`export default App`, imported without braces) and any number of **named exports** (`export function Button`, imported as `{ Button }`). *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Monorepo:** one repository with several apps and packages (web, admin, design system, shared utils), managed with workspaces (pnpm, npm, Yarn) and build tools like Turborepo or Nx. *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Mount / unmount:** a component appearing in the tree (created) / disappearing from it (destroyed, state lost). *(Section [24](#24-preserving-and-resetting-state-tree-position-and-keys))*
- **Mount / unmount (for effects):** the component appearing (effects set up) and disappearing (cleanups run). *(Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react))*
- **Mount / update / unmount (DOM):** creating a DOM node for a new element / changing an existing node / removing one. *(Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch))*
- **Moving creation inside:** create objects and functions inside the effect so they aren't unstable dependencies. *(Section [33](#33-separating-events-from-effects-useeffectevent-and-removing-dependencies))*
- **Moving state down:** putting fast-changing state in the smallest component that needs it, so siblings don't re-render. *(Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler))*
- **MSW (Mock Service Worker):** a library that defines **request handlers** (`http.get("/api/teas", () => HttpResponse.json([...]))`); in Node it hooks into `fetch` (`setupServer` from `msw/node`), in the browser it uses a Service Worker. Version 3 was released in September 2026. *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **Mutable:** a ref is meant to be mutated (unlike state, which you replace). *(Section [28](#28-refs-remembering-values-without-re-rendering))*
- **Mutating array methods:** `push`, `pop`, `shift`, `unshift`, `splice`, `sort`, `reverse`, `fill`, `copyWithin`, and index assignment `arr[i] = x`. *(Section [18](#18-updating-arrays-in-state))*
- **Mutation:** changing an object or array in place (`arr.push(x)`, `obj.n = 1`). React expects you **not** to mutate state; you create new objects instead (Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state)). *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules), [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state))*
- **`MutationObserver`:** a browser API that reports DOM changes; used below to count exactly what React changed. *(Section [15](#15-render-and-commit-what-happens-when-state-changes))*

### N

- **`name` attribute:** the field's key in `FormData` and in a "one handler for all fields" pattern. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **Naming updater arguments:** use the first letter of the state (`c => c + 1`) or `prev` (`prev => prev + 1`). *(Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions))*
- **Nearest provider wins:** providers can be nested; a deeper provider overrides an outer one for its subtree. *(Section [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply))*
- **Nested component definition bug:** defining a component inside another creates a **new type** every render, so React resets it every render. *(Section [24](#24-preserving-and-resetting-state-tree-position-and-keys))*
- **Nested routes and `<Outlet />`:** child routes render inside their parent's `<Outlet />`, so layouts are shared across pages. *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **Nested update:** copying every object on the path to a change: `{ ...user, address: { ...user.address, city } }`. *(Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state))*
- **Nesting vs defining inside:** you **use** components inside other components, but you **define** each one at the top level of a file, never inside another component's body. *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*
- **Next.js:** the most used **React framework**: React plus routing, server rendering and a server, made by Vercel (Part 9). *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **`next/link` / `next/image`:** client-side navigation with prefetching / automatic image optimisation. *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Node:** one item in the DOM tree: an element node (`<li>`), a text node (the words inside it), and others. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Node.js:** a program that runs JavaScript outside the browser; development tools (Vite, TypeScript, test runners) run on it. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **`node_modules`:** the folder where npm puts installed packages (never edit it, never commit it). *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **Non-mutating array methods:** `concat`, spread `[...]`, `filter`, `map`, `slice`, `toSorted`, `toReversed`, `toSpliced`, `with`; they return new arrays. *(Section [18](#18-updating-arrays-in-state))*
- **Non-null assertion (`!`):** `document.getElementById("root")!` tells TypeScript "this isn't null" (you take responsibility). *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **Non-reactive logic:** code that should run only when something else triggers it, but read the latest values when it does (event handlers, effect events). *(Section [33](#33-separating-events-from-effects-useeffectevent-and-removing-dependencies))*
- **Non-reactive value:** something that can't change between renders: module-level constants, imported functions, `useRef` objects and state setter functions; they don't need to be listed. *(Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode))*
- **Normalisation:** storing nested data **flat**, as a lookup by id (`{ [id]: { id, title, childIds } }`), like database tables; updates touch one entry instead of copying deep trees. *(Section [22](#22-choosing-the-state-structure))*
- **Notify parent anti-pattern:** calling `onChange` from an effect after updating local state; call it in the event handler instead, or lift the state up. *(Section [32](#32-you-might-not-need-an-effect))*
- **npm (Node Package Manager):** the tool and online registry for JavaScript libraries (**packages**). `npm install react` downloads React into your project. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **npx / `npm create`:** run a package's command without installing it permanently; `npm create vite@latest` runs Vite's project generator. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*

### O

- **Object / property:** a group of named values `{ name: "Chai", price: 180 }`; each name–value pair is a **property**, read with `obj.name`. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Object spread (`{ ...obj, key: value }`):** copies all properties into a new object, then overrides some; later properties win. *(Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state))*
- **Object type / `type` alias / `interface`:** describing an object's shape: `type Props = { name: string; price?: number }`; `interface Props { … }` does the same for objects. *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **`Object.is`:** the comparison React uses to decide whether state changed; for objects it is true only for the **same** object. *(Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state))*
- **`onChange`:** in React it fires on **every keystroke** for text inputs (like the DOM `input` event), not only when the field loses focus as the DOM's `change` event does. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **One-way data flow:** data moves **down** the tree through props; requests to change it move **up** through callbacks. *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **`onShellReady` / `onAllReady`:** callbacks: the shell can be sent / everything is rendered (bots and static generation wait for `onAllReady`). *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **`onSubmit` + `preventDefault()`:** handle the form's submit (Enter key or a submit button) without reloading the page. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **`onUnhandledRequest: "error"`:** makes any request without a handler fail the test, so nothing reaches a real server by accident. *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **Open source:** software whose code anyone can read, use and improve, usually for free. *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **Optimistic message:** showing the user's message instantly before the server confirms (Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic)). *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **Optimistic update:** updating the cache **before** the server confirms, rolling back on error. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **Optional property (`?`):** may be missing (its type includes `undefined`). *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **Out-of-order streaming:** each boundary's HTML is sent as soon as it's ready, in any order, inside a hidden `<div>`, then moved into place by an inline script (React's `$RC` "reveal completed" function). *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **Overscan:** extra rows rendered just outside the viewport so fast scrolling doesn't show blanks. *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **Owner stack (19.1):** the chain of components that rendered a component, for debugging (Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors)). *(Section [69](#69-whats-new-20222026-react-18-to-193-and-the-ecosystem))*
- **Owner stack (`captureOwnerStack`, React 19.1):** a development-only stack of the components that **rendered** (owned) the failing one, which is usually more useful than the parent chain. *(Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors))*

### P

- **`package.json`:** the project's manifest: its name, **scripts** (`npm run dev`) and **dependencies**. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **`page.tsx`:** the UI for a route; receives `params` and `searchParams` (both promises in Next.js 15+, so you `await` them). *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Pagination:** splitting data into pages; the server returns one page at a time (`?page=3&pageSize=20`, or a **cursor**). *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **Paint:** the browser drawing the updated DOM on screen, after the commit. *(Section [15](#15-render-and-commit-what-happens-when-state-changes))*
- **Paint / render (browser):** the browser turning the DOM plus CSS into pixels; changing the DOM makes it redo part of that work. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Parent / child / sibling:** in `<ul><li>A</li><li>B</li></ul>` the `ul` is the **parent** of both `li`s, they are its **children**, and they are **siblings** of each other. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **Parent / child component:** a component that renders another is its **parent**; the one rendered is the **child**. *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*
- **Partial prerendering (PPR):** prerendering a static shell of a page at build time and streaming the dynamic parts per request (Next.js Cache Components, Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching)). *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **PascalCase:** `ProductCard`: every word capitalised. React treats `<productCard>` (lowercase first letter) as an HTML tag, so components **must** start with a capital. *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*
- **Passing elements to avoid drilling:** the parent that owns the data creates the deep element itself and passes it **down as JSX** through the layout, so the middle layers never see the data. *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components))*
- **Passive effect vs layout effect:** `useEffect` (after paint) vs `useLayoutEffect` (before paint, synchronous after the commit). *(Section [72](#72-behaviour-questions-what-renders-what-logs-and-when))*
- **Patch:** a DOM operation that applies a difference: create, remove, move a node, set a property, change text. *(Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch))*
- **Path pattern / dynamic segment:** `/teas/:id` matches `/teas/7`, giving the **param** `id = "7"`; `*` matches anything (a "splat", used for 404 pages). *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **`play()` / `pause()`:** start and stop a `<video>` or `<audio>`. *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **Playwright:** Microsoft's browser automation and E2E framework: `page.goto`, `page.getByRole(...)`, `expect(locator).toHaveText(...)`, with automatic waiting. *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **Plural rules:** languages differ in how many plural forms they have (English: one/other; Arabic: zero/one/two/few/many/other); `Intl.PluralRules` tells you which form a number needs. *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Polling:** asking the server "anything new?" every few seconds (simple, wasteful, delayed). *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **Portal (`createPortal(children, domNode)`):** renders children into a different DOM node (often `document.body`) while they stay in the same place in the React tree (context and events still flow normally). *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **Position:** where a component sits among its parent's children (first child, second child…), regardless of variable names in your code. *(Section [24](#24-preserving-and-resetting-state-tree-position-and-keys))*
- **Preloading:** starting to download a chunk before it's needed (on hover, or with `<link rel="modulepreload">`). *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*
- **Premature optimisation:** optimising before measuring; often adds complexity for no visible gain. *(Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler))*
- **`prerender` / `prerenderToNodeStream` (`react-dom/static`):** waits for all data (Suspense) and returns complete HTML, for static generation. *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **Preserved state:** the same type at the same position across renders keeps its state. *(Section [24](#24-preserving-and-resetting-state-tree-position-and-keys))*
- **Preserving hidden state:** to keep state of something that's hidden, keep it rendered but hidden with CSS, lift its state up, or use `<Activity>` (Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition)). *(Section [24](#24-preserving-and-resetting-state-tree-position-and-keys))*
- **`preventDefault()`:** cancels the browser's default action, e.g. a form submit reloading the page. *(Section [13](#13-responding-to-events))*
- **Production build:** `vite build` / `next build` output: minified code, dead code removed, `process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"`. *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **Production error codes:** in production builds React shortens messages to a code with a link (`Minified React error #301`); the link expands it. *(Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors))*
- **`<Profiler id onRender>`:** a built-in component that reports how long its subtree took to render each time it commits (`actualDuration`) and what kind of commit it was (`phase`: `"mount"`, `"update"`, `"nested-update"`). *(Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler))*
- **Progressive enhancement:** with Server Functions (Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching)) the same form can submit before JavaScript loads. *(Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic))*
- **Project structure:** how folders and files are organised. *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Promise:** an object representing a value that isn't ready yet; it is **pending**, then either **fulfilled** (with a value) or **rejected** (with an error). Fulfilled or rejected = **settled**. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **`Promise.all`:** waits for several promises **in parallel** and gives all results (or the first error). *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **Prop:** one named input to a component, written like an HTML attribute: `name="Masala chai"`, `price={180}`. *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **Prop drilling:** passing a prop through many intermediate components that don't use it, only to reach a deep child. *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components), [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply))*
- **Prop types (TypeScript):** describing each prop's type, e.g. `{ name: string; price: number; onAdd?: () => void }`; the `?` marks an optional prop (Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children)). *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **Propagation in React:** React events bubble up the **component tree** (including through portals, Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals)); `e.stopPropagation()` stops parents' handlers from running. *(Section [13](#13-responding-to-events))*
- **Props object:** all of a component's props gathered into one object, the function's first (and only) parameter. *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **Provider:** the component that supplies a value to its subtree. In React 19 you render the context itself: `<ThemeContext value="dark">…</ThemeContext>` (older code: `<ThemeContext.Provider value=…>`). *(Section [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply))*
- **Provider component:** your own component (`TasksProvider`) that owns state and renders the context providers around `children`. *(Section [37](#37-scaling-up-with-reducer-and-context))*
- **`Provider`, `useSelector`, `useDispatch` (react-redux):** make the store available, read a slice, send actions. *(Section [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **`proxy.ts`:** code that runs before matching requests (redirects, rewrites, auth checks); renamed from `middleware.ts` in Next.js 16. *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Pseudo-localisation:** replacing text with accented, longer versions ("[Ǻđđ ŧǿ ƈȧřŧ]") during testing to find untranslated strings and layouts that break with longer text. *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Public API (index file):** a feature's `index.ts` that exports only what other features may use; everything else is private by convention or lint rule. *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Pure function:** a function that (1) returns the same output for the same input and (2) has no side effects. `double(x) = x * 2` is pure. *(Section [10](#10-keeping-components-pure))*
- **`PureComponent`:** a class that skips re-rendering when props and state are shallowly equal (like `memo`). *(Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*

### Q

- **Queries (Testing Library):** `getBy…` (exactly one, throws otherwise), `queryBy…` (returns `null` if missing), `findBy…` (waits, async), each with `…All…` variants. *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **Query key:** an array that uniquely identifies the data, like a cache address: `["teas"]`, `["tea", id]`, `["teas", { sort }]`. Different keys = different cache entries. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **Query priority:** prefer `getByRole` (with `name`), then `getByLabelText`, `getByPlaceholderText`, `getByText`, `getByDisplayValue`, `getByAltText`, `getByTitle`, and only then `getByTestId`. *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **`QueryClient` / `QueryClientProvider`:** the cache object and the provider that makes it available to components. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **`querySelector`:** finds the first element matching a selector: `document.querySelector(".price")`. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*

### R

- **Race condition:** a bug where the result depends on which of several async operations finishes first, e.g. an old, slow search response overwriting a newer one. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **Race condition (in fetching):** responses arriving out of order, so a stale response replaces a newer one. *(Section [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller))*
- **Race guard:** ignoring results from out-of-date async calls (Section [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller)). *(Section [70](#70-interview-coding-hooks-and-utilities-from-scratch))*
- **Re-render:** calling the component function again after state changes to get the new description of the UI. *(Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it), [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate))*
- **Re-render on change:** when a provider's `value` changes (compared with `Object.is`), **every** component that reads that context re-renders, even if it only uses part of the value. *(Section [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply))*
- **Re-render trigger:** what causes a component to render again (state, parent, context, store). *(Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler))*
- **Re-synchronisation:** stopping and restarting an effect because a dependency changed. *(Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode))*
- **React:** an open-source JavaScript library for building UIs from components, created at Facebook (now Meta) and open-sourced in 2013; since February 2026 it is owned by the independent React Foundation, hosted by the Linux Foundation. *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **React Compiler:** a build-time tool (`babel-plugin-react-compiler`, v1.0 released October 7, 2025) that analyses components and inserts fine-grained caching, so components re-run only the parts whose inputs changed. *(Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler))*
- **React DevTools:** a browser extension (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) with a **Components** tab (inspect and edit props, state and hooks of any component) and a **Profiler** tab (record renders, Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler)). *(Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors))*
- **React DevTools Profiler:** records commits in the browser and shows a flame chart, ranked chart and "why did this render?". *(Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler))*
- **React DOM:** the package that connects React to web pages. *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **React element:** the plain object a JSX expression produces: `{ type: "h1", props: { children: "Hi" }, key: null }`. Cheap to create and thrown away after each render. *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **React Foundation:** the independent, Linux Foundation-hosted organisation that owns React, React Native and JSX since February 2026 (announced October 2025). *(Section [69](#69-whats-new-20222026-react-18-to-193-and-the-ecosystem))*
- **React Hook Form (RHF):** `useForm()` returns `register` (connects an input), `handleSubmit` (validates then calls your function), `formState.errors`, `reset`, `watch`, and more. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **React Native:** the sibling that connects React to iPhone and Android screens instead. *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **React Performance tracks (React 19.2):** extra lanes in the browser's Performance panel showing React's scheduler and component renders. *(Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors))*
- **React Router 8 changes:** `react-router-dom` was removed (import from `react-router`, and `RouterProvider` from `react-router/dom` in the browser); ESM-only packages; Node 22.22+ and React 19.2.7+ required; middleware always on. *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **React Router modes:** **declarative** (`<BrowserRouter><Routes>`), **data** (`createBrowserRouter` with loaders and actions, Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui)) and **framework** (a full framework with server rendering and file-based routes, the successor of Remix). *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **`react-error-boundary`:** a popular library providing `<ErrorBoundary fallbackRender onReset resetKeys>` and `useErrorBoundary()`. *(Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors))*
- **`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`:** a lint rule (React Compiler rules in `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` 7) that flags synchronous `setState` calls inside effects. *(Section [32](#32-you-might-not-need-an-effect))*
- **Reactive logic:** code whose result should update when its inputs change (effects, rendering). *(Section [33](#33-separating-events-from-effects-useeffectevent-and-removing-dependencies))*
- **Reactive value:** props, state, and anything computed from them in the component body; they can change between renders, so effects that read them must list them. *(Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react))*
- **`ReactNode`:** the TypeScript type for anything renderable (elements, strings, numbers, arrays, `null`), used for `children` and slot props. *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components), [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **Read-only (immutable) props:** React freezes the props object in development, so assigning to it throws. *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **Read-only warning:** passing `value` without `onChange` makes a field the user can't type into; React warns in development. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **Reading primitives:** destructure the strings/numbers you need from an object prop **outside** the effect and depend on those. *(Section [33](#33-separating-events-from-effects-useeffectevent-and-removing-dependencies))*
- **Reading refs during render:** not allowed (except for one-time lazy initialisation), because the result wouldn't update the UI and breaks purity; read and write refs in event handlers and effects. *(Section [28](#28-refs-remembering-values-without-re-rendering))*
- **Reconciliation:** that comparing-and-updating process. *(Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it))*
- **Reconciliation / diffing:** comparing the new element tree with the previous one to work out the minimum DOM changes. *(Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch))*
- **Reconciliation by key:** when re-rendering a list, React pairs old and new children with the same key (keep and update), creates children with new keys, and removes children whose keys disappeared (Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch)). *(Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys))*
- **Reconnect with backoff:** retrying a dropped connection after increasing delays (1 s, 2 s, 4 s…). *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **Recoverable error / `onRecoverableError`:** errors React handles by falling back to client rendering, like mismatches; the root option lets you report them. *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*
- **Recursive component:** a component that renders itself for nested data (a file tree). *(Section [71](#71-machine-coding-round-classic-components-built-and-tested))*
- **Recursive rendering:** when a component re-renders, React also re-renders all of its children by default (whether or not their props changed); Section [44](#44-why-components-re-render-and-measuring-with-the-profiler) and Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler) cover skipping that. *(Section [15](#15-render-and-commit-what-happens-when-state-changes))*
- **`redirect(url)`:** returned or thrown from a loader/action to navigate somewhere else (e.g. after creating something). *(Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui))*
- **Reducer:** a pure function `(state, action) => nextState`. The name comes from `array.reduce`, which folds a list of values into one result the same way. *(Section [35](#35-usereducer-state-logic-in-one-place))*
- **Redundant state:** state that can be computed from other state or props (`fullName` from `firstName` + `lastName`); it goes stale when you forget to update it. *(Section [22](#22-choosing-the-state-structure))*
- **Redux:** the classic predictable-state library (one store, actions, reducers); **Redux Toolkit (RTK)** is the official modern way (`configureStore`, `createSlice`, Immer built in, RTK Query for server data). *(Section [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **Redux DevTools:** a browser extension showing every action and the state after it, with time-travel. *(Section [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **Ref:** a plain object `{ current: … }` that persists for the component's lifetime and can be changed freely. *(Section [28](#28-refs-remembering-values-without-re-rendering))*
- **`ref` as a prop (React 19):** function components can accept `ref` like any prop and pass it to an inner element. Older code needed `forwardRef` for this (still supported, being phased out). *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **Ref callback:** passing a **function** as `ref`: React calls it with the node when it attaches; since React 19 the function may **return a cleanup** function, called when the node detaches. *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **Ref vs state vs variable:** a local variable resets every render; state persists **and** re-renders; a ref persists **without** re-rendering. *(Section [28](#28-refs-remembering-values-without-re-rendering))*
- **`ref.current`:** the stored value; read and write it directly (`ref.current = 5`). *(Section [28](#28-refs-remembering-values-without-re-rendering))*
- **Reference vs value:** variables hold objects and arrays **by reference** (an arrow to the same object), so `a === b` is true only when both point to the **same** object, not when they merely look equal. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Referential equality:** two objects or functions are "equal" to `Object.is` only if they're the **same** object; `{} !== {}` and `(() => {}) !== (() => {})`. *(Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler))*
- **`register("field")`:** returns `name`, `ref`, `onChange` and `onBlur` props for an uncontrolled input. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **Removing a dependency:** changing the code so the effect no longer reads the value (not deleting it from the list). *(Section [33](#33-separating-events-from-effects-useeffectevent-and-removing-dependencies))*
- **Render (React):** calling component functions to compute JSX; pure and side-effect free (Section [10](#10-keeping-components-pure)). *(Section [15](#15-render-and-commit-what-happens-when-state-changes))*
- **Render order vs effect order:** components render top-down (parent, then children) but their effects run bottom-up (children first), after the whole tree has committed. *(Section [72](#72-behaviour-questions-what-renders-what-logs-and-when))*
- **Render phase:** the moment React calls your component to compute JSX; it must be pure. *(Section [10](#10-keeping-components-pure))*
- **Render prop:** a prop that is a **function returning JSX** (`renderItem={(item) => <Row … />}`), letting the parent decide how each part renders (more in Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props)). *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components), [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*
- **"Rendered more hooks than during the previous render":** React's error when a render calls more hooks than last time (a conditional hook became true). *(Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks))*
- **Renderer:** the package that turns React's decisions into a platform's operations (React DOM for the web, React Native for mobile). *(Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch))*
- **`renderHook`:** Testing Library's helper to test a hook by rendering a tiny component that calls it; `result.current` holds the latest return value. *(Section [38](#38-custom-hooks-reusing-stateful-logic), [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **Rendering a component:** React calling your component function to find out what it should show. *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*
- **`renderToPipeableStream` (Node) / `renderToReadableStream` (web streams):** React's streaming server APIs. *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **`renderToString(element)`:** React DOM's simplest server API: returns the HTML string synchronously (no streaming, no waiting for data). *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **Replace vs updater:** `setCount(5)` replaces the value; `setCount(c => c + 1)` is an **updater function** that receives the previous queued value and returns the next. *(Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions))*
- **Request handler / `server.use(...)`:** a rule matching a method and URL; `server.use` adds temporary handlers for one test (an error case, say). *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **Requirements clarification:** asking about scope before coding (keyboard support? API shape? mobile?). *(Section [71](#71-machine-coding-round-classic-components-built-and-tested))*
- **Reset:** clearing the boundary's error so it tries rendering its children again (a "Try again" button, or when `resetKeys` change). *(Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors))*
- **Reset (remount):** React destroys a component and its whole subtree's state and creates a fresh one: when its type changes, it's removed, or its key changes. *(Section [24](#24-preserving-and-resetting-state-tree-position-and-keys))*
- **Resolver (`zodResolver(schema)`):** an adapter that makes RHF validate with an external schema library. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **`response.ok`:** `true` for statuses 200–299. `fetch` does **not** reject on 404 or 500, so you must check it. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **Rest syntax (`...`):** the reverse: gathers "everything else": `const { id, ...rest } = item;`. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Returning `null`:** a component that returns `null` renders nothing (it still exists and runs). *(Section [11](#11-conditional-rendering))*
- **Revalidation:** after an action completes, the router re-runs the active loaders so every part of the page shows updated data. *(Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui))*
- **Role / accessible name:** what an element is (button, link, dialog) and what it's called (its label text); Testing Library's `getByRole(role, { name })` queries exactly this. *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **Root component:** the top of the tree, usually `App`, passed to `createRoot(...).render(...)`. *(Section [7](#7-your-first-component))*
- **Root element / `createRoot`:** the empty `<div id="root">` in `index.html`; `createRoot(element).render(<App />)` tells React to manage everything inside it. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **Root error callbacks (React 19):** `createRoot(el, { onCaughtError, onUncaughtError, onRecoverableError })` to report errors to monitoring. *(Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors))*
- **Route:** a mapping from a URL **path pattern** to a component (and optionally data functions). *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **Route `ErrorBoundary`:** a component shown when that route's loader, action or rendering throws. *(Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui))*
- **Route segment / dynamic segment:** each folder is a URL segment; `[id]` is dynamic (`params.id`), `[...slug]` catches all. *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Route-based splitting:** one chunk per page, the most effective split (React Router and Next.js do it for you). *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*
- **`route.ts` (Route Handler):** exports `GET`, `POST`… functions that return web `Response`s: an API endpoint inside the app. *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Roving tab index / arrow-key navigation:** moving focus or highlight between items with arrow keys while Tab moves out of the widget. *(Section [71](#71-machine-coding-round-classic-components-built-and-tested))*
- **RSC framework:** React defines RSC, but you need a bundler/framework integration to use it: Next.js App Router, React Router (RSC support is still marked unstable), Waku, Parcel. *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **RSC payload (Flight format):** the serialized tree a Server Component render produces: elements, text, and **client references** (pointers to client component modules), streamed to the browser. *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **RTL (right-to-left):** scripts written from right to left (Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu, Persian); the page sets `dir="rtl"` and the layout mirrors. *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Rules of Hooks:** (1) only call hooks at the top level of a function component or custom hook; (2) don't call them from regular functions, classes, event handlers, or after a conditional early `return`. *(Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks))*
- **Rules of Hooks lint rule (`rules-of-hooks`):** errors when hooks are called conditionally or in loops (Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks)). *(Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode))*
- **`rules-of-hooks` lint rule:** flags violations at edit time (Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode)). *(Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks))*
- **RUM (real-user monitoring):** collecting metrics from real users' browsers (with the `web-vitals` library) vs lab tests (Lighthouse) on one machine. *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*

### S

- **Same-type rule:** if an element has the same `type` (`"div"` or the same component function) at the same position, React keeps the DOM node or component instance and only updates props. *(Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch))*
- **Scheduler:** React's internal package that orders work by priority and decides when to yield. *(Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*
- **Schema:** a description of the expected data shape and rules: `z.object({ email: z.email(), qty: z.number().min(1) })`. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **Screen reader:** software that reads the UI aloud (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS, TalkBack) using the **accessibility tree** the browser builds from your HTML. *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **`scrollIntoView()`:** scrolls the page or container so an element is visible. *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **`scrollTop`:** how many pixels a container has been scrolled down. *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **Search params (query string):** `?q=chai&sort=price`; URL state that's bookmarkable and shareable. *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **`<select>` / `<textarea>` / checkbox / radio:** in React a `select` and `textarea` use `value` (not `selected` or inner text); checkboxes and radios use `checked`. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **Selected id pattern:** store `selectedId` and look the object up in the list during render. *(Section [22](#22-choosing-the-state-structure))*
- **Selective / progressive hydration:** with Suspense, React hydrates parts of the page independently, prioritising what the user interacts with. *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*
- **Selective hydration:** hydrating each streamed part independently; parts the user clicks on are hydrated first. *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **Selector:** the part of a CSS rule (or a JavaScript query) that picks elements: `p`, `.price` (class), `#cart` (id), `ul > li`. *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events), [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **Semantic HTML:** elements that describe their meaning (`button`, `nav`, `main`, `h1`–`h6`, `ul`, `label`) instead of generic `div`s. *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **Semantic versioning (semver):** versions written `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (19.3.1); `^19.2.8` in `package.json` means "19.2.8 or any later 19.x". *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **SEO (search engine optimisation):** making pages easy for search engines to index; server-rendered HTML is easier to index and to preview on social media. *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **Serializable props:** props passed from a Server to a Client Component must be serializable (strings, numbers, plain objects, arrays, Dates, promises, JSX); not functions (except Server Functions) or class instances. *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **Server Component:** the default kind of component in an RSC framework; runs on the server, may be `async`, can't use state, effects or browser APIs; its code isn't in the client bundle. *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **Server Function (`"use server"`):** an async function that runs on the server but can be called from the client (as a form action or directly); the client gets a reference id, not the code. Formerly called "Server Actions" when used with forms. *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **Server state:** data owned by a server that your UI shows a copy of; it can go stale and needs refetching (Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query)). *(Section [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller), [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **Server-Sent Events (SSE):** a one-way stream from server to client over HTTP (`Content-Type: text/event-stream`), with lines like `data: {…}` separated by blank lines; the browser's `EventSource` reconnects automatically. *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **Setter (set function):** `setCount(5)` or `setCount(c => c + 1)`; stores the next value and queues a re-render. *(Section [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate))*
- **Setup file:** code run before each test file (adding jest-dom matchers, cleaning up after each test). *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **Shallow array copy:** `[...arr]` copies the list of references; the objects inside are the **same** objects as before. *(Section [18](#18-updating-arrays-in-state))*
- **Shallow copy:** a copy of the outer object only; nested objects inside are still **shared** with the original. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Sharing logic vs sharing state:** each call to a hook creates independent state; to share state itself, lift it up or use context. *(Section [38](#38-custom-hooks-reusing-stateful-logic))*
- **Shell:** the parts of the page outside any pending Suspense boundary (layout, header, fallbacks); sent first. *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **Sibling uniqueness:** keys only need to be unique among siblings in the same list, not across the whole app. *(Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys))*
- **Side effect:** anything a function does besides returning a value: changing a variable outside it, writing to the DOM, `fetch`, `console.log`, timers, `localStorage`. *(Section [10](#10-keeping-components-pure))*
- **Side effect vs effect:** "side effect" is any change outside a function; an **Effect** (capital E in React docs) is specifically a side effect caused by rendering, not by a particular user action. *(Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react))*
- **Single responsibility principle:** a component should ideally do one thing; if it grows, split it. *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **Single source of truth:** one owner per piece of state; other components read it via props instead of keeping their own copies. *(Section [23](#23-sharing-state-lifting-state-up-and-a-single-source-of-truth))*
- **Single-page application (SPA):** a site that loads one HTML page and then updates it with JavaScript instead of loading new pages from the server. *(Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it))*
- **Slice (RTK):** a reducer plus its action creators for one area of state (`cartSlice`). *(Section [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **Slot (named slot):** a prop that receives JSX for a specific place: `<Layout sidebar={<Nav />} main={<Feed />} />`. *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components))*
- **Snapshot:** the values of props and state as they were for one particular render; event handlers created in that render see those values forever, even later (in a timeout). *(Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions), [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **Source map:** a file that maps bundled, minified code back to your original source, so stack traces and breakpoints point at your files. *(Section [41](#41-debugging-react-devtools-strict-mode-and-reading-errors), [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **Source of truth:** the one place a piece of data lives; everything else reads or derives from it. *(Section [22](#22-choosing-the-state-structure))*
- **SPA fallback:** for a client-side-routed app, the server returns `index.html` for unknown paths so deep links work. *(Section [68](#68-production-web-vitals-monitoring-builds-and-deployment))*
- **Spacer:** an element with the full list height (`count × rowHeight`) that gives the scrollbar its size; visible rows are absolutely positioned inside it. *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **Specialisation:** making a specific component by configuring a generic one (`WelcomeDialog` renders `Dialog` with fixed title). *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components))*
- **Specificity:** CSS's rules for which style wins when several apply; scoped approaches (Modules, Tailwind) avoid most specificity fights. *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js))*
- **Spread syntax (`...`):** copies the items of an array or properties of an object into a new one: `[...list, 4]`, `{ ...user, age: 31 }`. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Spreading props:** `<Avatar {...person} />` passes every property of `person` as a prop; handy but hides what's passed. *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **SSG (static site generation) / prerendering:** rendering pages to HTML files at build time. *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **SSR (server-side rendering):** the server renders HTML for each request, then the browser **hydrates** it (Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches)). *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **Stable callback:** a function whose identity doesn't change between renders, so effects and memoised children don't re-run. *(Section [70](#70-interview-coding-hooks-and-utilities-from-scratch))*
- **Stable key:** a key that stays the same for the same item across renders (a database id, a slug, a UUID created when the item was created). *(Section [12](#12-rendering-lists-and-keys))*
- **Stack reconciler:** React's pre-16 engine, which rendered recursively and couldn't stop once started. *(Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*
- **Stale closure:** an effect (or callback) that captured old values from an earlier render because it wasn't re-run when they changed. *(Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode))*
- **Stale UI indicator:** dimming content while `isPending` or while `value !== deferredValue`. *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **Stale value / stale closure:** a handler or timer that still sees an old snapshot because it was created during an earlier render. *(Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions))*
- **`staleTime`:** how long fetched data counts as fresh; while fresh, no refetch happens. Default `0` (stale immediately; refetched on mount, window focus or reconnect). *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **`startTransition` (standalone):** the same, without `isPending`, usable outside components. *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **State:** data that changes while the app runs (the cart's items, the text in a search box, whether a menu is open). *(Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it), [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate))*
- **State context / dispatch context:** two separate contexts; `dispatch` never changes identity, so components that only dispatch don't re-render when state changes. *(Section [37](#37-scaling-up-with-reducer-and-context))*
- **State machine (finite-state machine):** a model with a fixed list of states and the **events** (transitions) allowed from each; the UI is always in exactly one state. *(Section [21](#21-reacting-to-input-with-state-ui-as-a-state-machine))*
- **Stateful vs stateless component:** one that has state vs one that only uses props. *(Section [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate))*
- **Static version:** a first build that renders the data with props only, no state, so the structure is right before any interactivity. *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **Status variable / union type:** one variable such as `status: "typing" | "submitting" | "success" | "error"`, described in TypeScript as a **union of string literals**. *(Section [21](#21-reacting-to-input-with-state-ui-as-a-state-machine))*
- **Store:** a single object holding app state plus a way to update it; reducer + context is a do-it-yourself store. *(Section [37](#37-scaling-up-with-reducer-and-context), [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **Storybook:** a tool to develop and document components in isolation, one "story" per state. *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Storybook-style "living styleguide":** a page that renders a component in every state at once, so you can see and test each one (Storybook is the popular tool for this). *(Section [21](#21-reacting-to-input-with-state-ui-as-a-state-machine))*
- **Streaming:** sending a response in pieces (**chunks**) over one open connection instead of all at once. *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **Streaming response / `ReadableStream`:** a `fetch` response body read chunk by chunk with `response.body.getReader()` and a `TextDecoder`. *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **`StrictMode`:** a development-only wrapper that runs extra checks (it renders components twice and runs effects twice to expose bugs; Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode)). *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **`StrictMode` double render:** in development, React renders each component **twice** and compares, to surface impure components; production renders once. *(Section [10](#10-keeping-components-pure))*
- **StrictMode effect double-run:** in development React runs setup → cleanup → setup once on mount, to prove your cleanup works (Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode)). *(Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react))*
- **String vs expression prop:** `name="Chai"` passes a string; anything else (numbers, booleans, objects, functions, JSX) goes in braces: `price={180}`, `tags={["tea"]}`, `onAdd={handleAdd}`. *(Section [9](#9-props-passing-data-to-components))*
- **Structural sharing:** a new object reuses (points to) unchanged parts of the old one, so copying is cheap. *(Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state))*
- **`structuredClone`:** a built-in deep copy; rarely the right tool for state (it copies everything, breaking structural sharing). *(Section [18](#18-updating-arrays-in-state))*
- **`style` object:** inline styles are objects with camelCase CSS properties: `style={{ fontSize: 14, backgroundColor: "teal" }}` (numbers become pixels for most properties). *(Section [8](#8-jsx-markup-inside-javascript-and-what-it-compiles-to))*
- **`suppressHydrationWarning`:** an attribute that silences the mismatch warning for **one element's text/attributes** that legitimately differ (a timestamp); it doesn't fix deeper differences. *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*
- **Suspend / suspension:** a component signalling "I'm not ready yet" while waiting for code or data; the nearest Suspense boundary shows its fallback. *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*
- **Suspense boundary on the server:** where React can pause; a component that's waiting for data (it **suspends**) is replaced by its boundary's fallback in the shell. *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **`<Suspense fallback>`:** a boundary that shows `fallback` while anything inside it is suspended. *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*
- **SWR:** "stale-while-revalidate", also the name of Vercel's smaller alternative library. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **Synchronising state (anti-pattern):** keeping two copies of the same state in two components and trying to keep them equal with effects or callbacks. *(Section [23](#23-sharing-state-lifting-state-up-and-a-single-source-of-truth))*
- **Synchronous / asynchronous:** synchronous code runs line by line, each line finishing before the next; asynchronous work finishes **later**, while other code keeps running. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **SyntheticEvent:** React's wrapper around the browser's event object, with the same main properties (`target`, `currentTarget`, `preventDefault()`, `stopPropagation()`) working the same way in every browser. The original is at `event.nativeEvent`. *(Section [13](#13-responding-to-events))*

### T

- **Tag / element:** `<p>` is an opening **tag** and `</p>` a closing tag; together with what's between them they form an **element**. Some elements have no content and no closing tag (`<img>`, `<input>`, `<br>`). *(Section [2](#2-how-a-web-page-works-html-css-the-dom-and-events))*
- **TanStack Virtual / react-window / react-virtuoso:** popular virtualisation libraries. *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **Task (macrotask) / microtask:** two queues of waiting callbacks. Timers, clicks and network events are **tasks**; promise callbacks (`then`, code after `await`) are **microtasks**, and all waiting microtasks run before the next task. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **Tearing:** different parts of the UI showing different versions of the same external data during one render; `useSyncExternalStore` prevents it. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **Template literal:** a string in backticks that can embed values: `` `₹${price}` ``. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Ternary in JSX:** `{inStock ? <AddButton /> : <SoldOut />}`. *(Section [11](#11-conditional-rendering))*
- **Ternary operator:** `condition ? a : b` (an `if/else` that produces a value). *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **`test` / `describe` / `expect`:** define a test / group tests / make an assertion (`expect(x).toBe(3)`). *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **Test environment:** where tests run: `jsdom` (a simulated browser in Node, the usual choice for components), `happy-dom` (a faster alternative), or a real browser (Vitest Browser Mode, Playwright). *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **Test runner:** the program that finds test files, runs them and reports results; **Vitest** is the Vite-native runner (Jest-compatible API), **Jest** the older standard. *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **Testing Library (`render`, `screen`, `fireEvent`):** helpers to render a component into jsdom (`render`), find things on the page as a user would (`screen.getByRole("button")`, `screen.getByText(...)`), and fire events (`fireEvent.click(button)`). Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event) covers it properly. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **Testing trophy / pyramid:** guidance on how many tests of each kind: static checks, unit, **integration** (most valuable for UI), end-to-end. *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **`then` / `catch` / `finally`:** methods that register callbacks for when a promise fulfils, rejects, or settles either way. *(Section [4](#4-asynchronous-javascript-for-react-promises-asyncawait-and-fetch))*
- **`this.props` / `this.state`:** props and state on the instance; state is always one object. *(Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*
- **`this.setState(partial | updater, callback?)`:** merges the partial object into state (unlike `useState`, which replaces), batches, and can run a callback after the update. *(Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*
- **Throttle:** run a function at most once every `wait` ms (scroll and resize handlers). *(Section [70](#70-interview-coding-hooks-and-utilities-from-scratch))*
- **Time to first byte vs time to content:** streaming makes the first byte (and the shell) arrive early even when some data is slow. *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **Time zone:** the region whose clock rules apply (`Asia/Kolkata`); the same instant shows different local times, and server and client may disagree (a hydration risk, Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches)). *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Token streaming:** LLM APIs send their answer as small pieces of text (tokens) as they're generated; showing them immediately makes waiting feel shorter. *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **Top-down vs bottom-up:** building from the outer components inwards vs from the smallest pieces upwards; small apps usually go top-down, big apps bottom-up. *(Section [20](#20-thinking-in-react-from-mockup-to-components))*
- **`toSorted` / `toReversed` / `with`:** newer (ES2023) array methods that return a changed **copy** instead of mutating, perfect for React state. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Transition:** moving from one state to another in response to an event: `typing --submit--> submitting`. *(Section [21](#21-reacting-to-input-with-state-ui-as-a-state-machine))*
- **Transition (non-urgent update):** an update that can be interrupted and doesn't need to show instantly (filtering, switching tabs, navigation). *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **Transitions render independently (React 19.3):** a slow transition no longer holds up unrelated transitions. *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **Translation key / message catalogue:** a stable identifier (`"cart.items"`) mapped to the text in each language, usually stored in one JSON file per locale. *(Section [65](#65-internationalisation-translations-plurals-dates-numbers-and-right-to-left-layouts))*
- **Tree shaking:** the bundler removing code that's never imported/used. *(Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size))*
- **Trigger:** what starts a render: the initial `root.render(...)`, or a state setter being called (in this component or an ancestor). *(Section [15](#15-render-and-commit-what-happens-when-state-changes))*
- **Truthy / falsy:** values treated as `true` or `false` in conditions. The falsy ones are `false`, `0`, `""`, `null`, `undefined` and `NaN`; everything else is truthy. *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Truthy / falsy pitfall:** `{count && <p>{count} items</p>}` renders `0` when count is 0, because `0` is falsy but is a renderable number. ✅ `{count > 0 && …}`. *(Section [11](#11-conditional-rendering))*
- **`tsc` / type check:** the TypeScript compiler; `tsc --noEmit` checks types without producing files. *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **`.tsx` file:** a TypeScript file that may contain JSX. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*
- **TTFB (time to first byte):** how long until the browser receives the first byte of the response. *(Section [58](#58-rendering-strategies-csr-ssr-ssg-and-isr))*
- **TTI (time to interactive):** when the page is fully usable; with SSR it's after hydration. *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*
- **Turbopack:** Next.js's Rust-based bundler, the default for `next dev` and `next build` since Next.js 16. *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Two-pass rendering:** render a placeholder on the server and the first client render, then switch to client-only content in an effect (`useEffect(() => setMounted(true), [])`). *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*
- **Type annotation:** `: string` after a name tells TypeScript its type: `function f(name: string)`. *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **Type inference:** TypeScript working out types itself: `useState(0)` → `number`. *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **TypeScript:** JavaScript with **types** (labels such as "this is a number") that catch mistakes before the code runs; most React teams use it, and so do these notes (Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children)). *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*

### U

- **UI = f(state):** React's core idea: the screen is the output of a function of the state. Same state in, same UI out. *(Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it))*
- **UI tree / render tree:** the tree of components React builds from your JSX; state is attached to positions in it. *(Section [24](#24-preserving-and-resetting-state-tree-position-and-keys))*
- **Uncontrolled component:** an input that manages its own value in the DOM; you give a starting value with `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked` and read it later. *(Section [19](#19-forms-controlled-and-uncontrolled-inputs))*
- **Uncontrolled component (general sense):** a component that keeps its own internal state; easier to drop in, harder to coordinate. *(Section [23](#23-sharing-state-lifting-state-up-and-a-single-source-of-truth))*
- **Union type (`A | B`):** one of several types: `"sm" | "md" | "lg"`, `string | null`. *(Section [26](#26-typescript-with-react-typing-props-state-events-and-children))*
- **Unit of work:** processing one fiber (calling its component or updating its element); React works through the tree one unit at a time. *(Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*
- **`UNSAFE_` lifecycles:** `componentWillMount`, `componentWillReceiveProps`, `componentWillUpdate`: deprecated, prefixed `UNSAFE_`, unsafe with concurrent rendering. *(Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*
- **Unstable dependency:** an object or function created during render (`const options = {…}`); it's a **new** value each render, so an effect depending on it re-runs every time. *(Section [31](#31-the-lifecycle-of-an-effect-dependencies-cleanup-and-strict-mode))*
- **Unstable prop:** an object, array or function created during render and passed to a child, which defeats `memo`. *(Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler))*
- **Update queue:** the list of pending updates React keeps per state variable; processed in order during the next render. *(Section [16](#16-state-as-a-snapshot-batching-and-updater-functions))*
- **Updater function trick:** `setCount(c => c + 1)` inside an interval needs no `count` dependency. *(Section [33](#33-separating-events-from-effects-useeffectevent-and-removing-dependencies))*
- **`updateTag(tag)` / `revalidateTag(tag)`:** expire cached entries with a tag immediately (read-your-own-writes after a Server Function) / in the background. *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **Updating an object inside an array:** `map` over the array and return `{ ...item, field: value }` for the matching item. *(Section [18](#18-updating-arrays-in-state))*
- **Urgent update:** typing, clicking, pressing: users expect immediate feedback; rendered synchronously. *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **`"use cache"` + `cacheLife` + `cacheTag`:** cache a component's or function's result, for how long, with which tags. *(Section [62](#62-nextjs-app-router-layouts-server-functions-and-caching))*
- **`"use client"` directive:** marks a module as a boundary: from here down, components are client components. *(Section [61](#61-react-server-components-how-they-work))*
- **`use` exception:** React 19's `use` (for promises and context) isn't a hook in this sense and may be called conditionally. *(Section [39](#39-how-hooks-work-inside-build-usestate-from-scratch-and-the-rules-of-hooks))*
- **`use` prefix rule:** the name tells React's linter to apply the Rules of Hooks inside it and to its callers; a function that calls no hooks shouldn't start with `use`. *(Section [38](#38-custom-hooks-reusing-stateful-logic))*
- **`use(Context)`:** React 19's `use` can also read context and, unlike hooks, may be called inside conditions and loops. *(Section [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply))*
- **`use(promise)`:** reads a promise's value during render, suspending until it resolves (works on the server and the client). *(Section [60](#60-streaming-ssr-with-suspense))*
- **`useActionState(action, initialState)`:** returns `[state, formAction, isPending]`; your action receives `(previousState, formData)` and returns the next state. *(Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic))*
- **`useCallback(fn, deps)`:** returns the same function object until a dependency changes; equivalent to `useMemo(() => fn, deps)`. *(Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler))*
- **`useContext(Context)`:** reads the value from the nearest provider above; returns the **default value** if there's none. *(Section [36](#36-context-passing-data-deeply))*
- **`useDebugValue`:** labels a custom hook's value in React DevTools. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **`useDeferredValue(value)`:** returns the previous value during urgent renders and re-renders with the new value in the background; ideal when you don't control the state update (a prop). *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **`useEffect(setup, dependencies?)`:** registers an effect. `setup` may return a **cleanup** function. *(Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react))*
- **`useEffectEvent(fn)`:** returns a function you call **from inside effects**; it always sees the latest props and state, and it must **not** be listed as a dependency. Stable since React 19.2 (October 2025). *(Section [33](#33-separating-events-from-effects-useeffectevent-and-removing-dependencies))*
- **`useErrorBoundary().showBoundary(error)`:** passes an error from a handler or async code to the nearest boundary. *(Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors))*
- **`useFetcher()`:** submits or loads **without** navigating (a "like" button, an inline edit), with its own `state`. *(Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui))*
- **`useFormStatus()`:** from `react-dom`; returns `{ pending, data, method, action }` for the **parent** `<form>` of the component calling it. *(Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic))*
- **`useId`:** generates ids that match between server and client (Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop)). *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*
- **`useId()`:** returns a unique, stable string per component instance (React 19.2 format: `_r_0_`-style), identical in server-rendered HTML and on the client. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **`useImmerReducer`:** a version from `use-immer` that lets the reducer "mutate" a draft (Section [17](#17-updating-objects-in-state)). *(Section [35](#35-usereducer-state-logic-in-one-place))*
- **`useImperativeHandle`:** limits what a parent can do through a ref to a few methods you choose (Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop)). *(Section [29](#29-refs-to-dom-elements-focus-scroll-measure-and-media))*
- **`useImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({ … }))`:** exposes a custom object (e.g. `{ focus, clear }`) through a ref instead of the raw DOM node. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **`useInsertionEffect`:** for CSS-in-JS libraries to inject styles before layout effects; not for app code. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **`useLayoutEffect`:** like `useEffect`, but runs synchronously after the commit and before paint; blocks painting, so use it only for measuring and immediately adjusting layout. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **`useMemo(() => compute(a, b), [a, b])`:** returns the cached value until `a` or `b` changes. *(Section [45](#45-memo-usememo-usecallback-and-the-react-compiler))*
- **`useMutation`:** runs a change (POST/PUT/DELETE) with its own pending/error state. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **`useNavigation()`:** the global navigation state: `"idle"`, `"loading"` (a navigation's loaders are running) or `"submitting"` (an action is running). *(Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui))*
- **`useOptimistic(state, updateFn?)`:** returns a value that shows the optimistic version while an action is pending and automatically falls back to the real state when it finishes. *(Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic))*
- **`useParams()` / `useSearchParams()` / `useNavigate()` / `useLocation()`:** read path params / read and set the query string / navigate from code / read the current location. *(Section [50](#50-routing-with-react-router-urls-params-and-nested-layouts))*
- **`useQuery({ queryKey, queryFn })`:** subscribes a component to cached data; returns `data`, `error`, `status` (`"pending"`, `"error"`, `"success"`) and `isFetching`. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **User interface (UI):** everything a person sees and interacts with in an app: text, buttons, inputs, menus, pages. *(Section [1](#1-how-to-use-these-notes-and-what-a-react-developer-does))*
- **`user-event`:** simulates full interactions (`await user.type(input, "chai")` fires focus, keydown, input, keyup… for each character), more realistic than `fireEvent`, which dispatches one event. *(Section [56](#56-testing-components-vitest-testing-library-and-user-event))*
- **`useReducer(reducer, initialArg, init?)`:** returns `[state, dispatch]`; the optional `init` function computes the initial state lazily. *(Section [35](#35-usereducer-state-logic-in-one-place))*
- **`useRef(initial)`:** returns the same ref object on every render; `initial` is used only on the first. *(Section [28](#28-refs-remembering-values-without-re-rendering))*
- **`useShallow`:** Zustand helper for selecting several values as an object without re-rendering when other parts change. *(Section [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **`useState(initial)`:** declares a state variable; returns a pair `[value, setValue]` (array destructuring lets you name them). *(Section [14](#14-state-a-components-memory-usestate))*
- **`useSuspenseQuery`:** a version that suspends (Section [47](#47-code-splitting-lazy-suspense-and-bundle-size)) instead of returning a pending status. *(Section [52](#52-server-state-with-tanstack-query))*
- **`useSyncExternalStore`'s `getServerSnapshot`:** gives a server-safe value for external data during hydration. *(Section [59](#59-hydration-and-hydration-mismatches))*
