- **`useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot?)`:** reads a value from an external store and re-renders when the store changes, safely under concurrent rendering. *(Section [40](#40-more-hooks-uselayouteffect-useid-usesyncexternalstore-useimperativehandle-and-ref-as-a-prop))*
- **`useTransition()`:** returns `[isPending, startTransition]`; updates inside `startTransition(() => …)` are transitions; `isPending` is true until they commit. Since React 19 the function can be `async` (an **action**, Section [53](#53-react-19-forms-actions-useactionstate-useformstatus-and-useoptimistic)). *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **Utility-first CSS / Tailwind CSS:** many tiny single-purpose classes (`p-4`, `rounded-xl`, `text-green-700`) combined in `className`; Tailwind scans your files and generates only the classes you use. *(Section [27](#27-styling-react-apps-css-css-modules-tailwind-and-css-in-js))*

### V

- **Validation:** checking that input meets rules (required, format, range) before using it. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **Validation mode:** when RHF validates: on submit (default), on blur, on change, or "on touched". *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **Variable (`const` / `let`):** a name for a value. `const` can't be reassigned (use it by default); `let` can. (Old `var` has confusing scoping; don't use it.) *(Section [3](#3-the-javascript-react-uses-arrow-functions-destructuring-spread-array-methods-and-modules))*
- **Variants:** a component's predefined visual options (`variant="primary" | "ghost"`, `size="sm" | "md"`), often defined with a helper such as `class-variance-authority` (cva). *(Section [66](#66-architecture-project-structure-design-systems-and-monorepos))*
- **Vercel AI SDK (`ai`, `@ai-sdk/react`):** a TypeScript toolkit for LLM apps; `useChat` manages messages, streaming status and sending, using a **UI message stream** protocol over SSE. Version 7 (June 2026) is current. *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **View Transitions API:** a browser feature (`document.startViewTransition`) that animates between two DOM states with CSS. *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **Viewport:** the visible part of a scrolling container. *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **`<ViewTransition>`:** React 19.3's component that triggers view transitions for its children when they change **inside a transition** (or a deferred value, or a Suspense reveal); `addTransitionType(type)` labels a transition so CSS can animate differently (e.g. "forward" vs "back"). *(Section [63](#63-transitions-usetransition-usedeferredvalue-activity-and-viewtransition))*
- **Virtual DOM:** React's lightweight description of the UI (plain JavaScript objects). React compares the new description with the previous one and changes only the real DOM nodes that differ (Section [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch)). *(Section [5](#5-why-react-updating-a-page-by-hand-vs-describing-it), [42](#42-the-virtual-dom-and-reconciliation-build-a-mini-react-from-scratch))*
- **Virtualisation / windowing:** rendering only the visible slice of a long list and swapping rows as the user scrolls. *(Section [46](#46-long-lists-virtualisation-and-pagination))*
- **Visual state:** one distinct way the UI looks (form empty / being submitted / succeeded / failed). *(Section [21](#21-reacting-to-input-with-state-ui-as-a-state-machine))*
- **Vite:** the standard build tool for React apps: a **dev server** with instant reloads, and a production **build**. *(Section [6](#6-setting-up-node-npm-vite-and-how-these-examples-run))*

### W

- **Waterfall:** requests that run one after another because each component only starts fetching after its parent rendered; slow on real networks. *(Section [34](#34-fetching-data-in-effects-loading-errors-race-conditions-and-abortcontroller))*
- **Waterfall vs parallel loading:** fetching in nested components' effects runs one level after another; route loaders for all matches start together. *(Section [51](#51-router-data-loaders-actions-and-pending-ui))*
- **WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines):** the standard (version 2.2) most laws and audits refer to; AA is the usual target level. *(Section [49](#49-accessibility-semantics-focus-aria-portals-and-modals))*
- **`webServer` (Playwright config):** starts your app (e.g. `vite preview`) before the tests and stops it after. *(Section [57](#57-testing-data-and-flows-msw-hooks-and-playwright-end-to-end))*
- **WebSocket:** a long-lived, two-way connection (`new WebSocket("wss://…")`) for messages in both directions with low latency. *(Section [64](#64-real-time-and-streaming-uis-websockets-sse-and-ai-chat))*
- **What isn't caught:** errors in event handlers, timers and promises (they don't happen during rendering), server-side rendering errors, and errors inside the boundary itself. *(Section [48](#48-error-boundaries-handling-render-errors))*
- **Where side effects go:** in **event handlers** (Section [13](#13-responding-to-events)) for things caused by a user action, or in **effects** (Section [30](#30-effects-synchronising-with-systems-outside-react)) for synchronising with outside systems after rendering. *(Section [10](#10-keeping-components-pure))*
- **Where state belongs:** server data → TanStack Query; URL state → router; form drafts → the form library; truly global UI state → a store or context. *(Section [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*
- **Work loop:** the loop that performs units of work; the interruptible version checks after each unit whether it should **yield**. *(Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*
- **Wrapper component:** wraps children to add behaviour or styling (`<Tooltip text="…"><button/></Tooltip>`). *(Section [25](#25-composition-children-slots-and-layout-components))*
- **Wrapper hell:** deeply nested HOCs and render props, the problem hooks solved. *(Section [67](#67-legacy-react-class-components-lifecycles-hocs-and-render-props))*

### X

- **XState:** a library for complex state machines and statecharts in JavaScript; useful for multi-step flows, overkill for a single form. *(Section [21](#21-reacting-to-input-with-state-ui-as-a-state-machine))*

### Y

- **Yielding / time slicing:** pausing rendering after a few milliseconds (about 5 ms in React's scheduler) so the browser can handle input and paint, then continuing. *(Section [43](#43-fiber-scheduling-and-concurrent-rendering))*

### Z

- **`z.infer<typeof schema>`:** the TypeScript type derived from a schema, so types and runtime rules can't drift apart. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **Zod:** a TypeScript-first schema library; `schema.parse(x)` returns typed data or throws, `schema.safeParse(x)` returns `{ success, data | error }`. Zod 4 (2025) made it faster and added top-level formats like `z.email()`. *(Section [54](#54-form-libraries-react-hook-form-and-zod-validation))*
- **Zustand:** a tiny store library: `create((set) => ({ ...state, ...actions }))` returns a hook you call with a selector. *(Section [55](#55-global-state-build-a-store-then-zustand-redux-toolkit-and-jotai))*

---
